EventNotes:

Race day reg here


 

Sorry Honey, I've gotta work late! 

REGISTRATION:
We encourage racers to register early.  We are offering series entry, at a discount, or you can sign up for individual event dates.

COURSE INFO:
All races will be located in Forest Hill Park, Richmond, VA. 

Cross course: the lap will be approximately one mile in length using a combination of surfaces that may include grass, blacktop and dirt.   What type of bike?  We don't care...race your cross, mountain or gravel bike. 

Lapped Rider:  If you are lapped you can continue to race, unlike some cyclo cross races. Once the race leader finishes the required number of laps, remaining riders will will be done once they complete their current lap.  The event will be scored by number of laps completed, then by time.

AWARDS: 
There will be series awards after 3rd race.  To be eligible for prizes, you must enter and race all three events.  

DISTANCE/TIME:
All races will be about 45 minutes.  Our goal is for the 1st pace overall to race close to 45 minutes.  All racers then will finish their current lap once the leader finishes. There will be a countdown lap count at the start/finish.  Lapped racers will not be removed from the course!  All racers will be able to continue to the finish of the event!

NUMBER OF LAPS:
Race organizers will determine numbers of laps based on average time per lap of leaders.  Once laps times are established there will be l lap counter counting down the laps.  This number will be reduced by 1 each time the leader crosses the line.  Note that the number can change by 2 if the leader passes you during any given lap. We will ring a bell for riders to signal "one to go". Historically, the winner completes 11 to 12 laps in the 45 minute window.

 

DONATION:
Donations will go to the local trail working groups (RVA MORE) earmarked to maintain the trails at Forest Hill Park.  Please donate a few bucks during registration.

RAIN OR WET CONDITIONS
To protect/secure our use of the park, we will postpone or cancel a race in the event of rain or wet conditions.  Don't let this prevent you from registering early.  We are happy to transfer fees to another runriderace event.

Course set up
I will be out at the course by early afternoon.  If you are able to come, shoot me an email letting me know you can come and your cell for contact.  We will probably need help right up to race start.

Race Numbers are reused for the WHOLE SERIES, if you lose or forget your race number, it will cost $5 paid in cash/Venmo each time you need a new one.

Prizes will be provided by Northampton Bicycle to the top 3 in each race.

EventNotes:
We are so excited for your child to participate in NICA Discovery! 

 

All NICA Discovery adult leaders are background checked and hold a coaching license from NICA.  There will always be at least 2 leaders who have current first aid training. 

 

  • New Friends is the introductory level and is aimed at children who are new to biking but have some limited experience with neighborhood or urban riding.  These are children who can already balance and pedal a bike, but may have never ventured “off road.” Games and activities work on learning to better ride and operate a bike preparation for later buildable skills, and increasing stamina.

 

Participants must be able to ride a bike confidently before joining a program and must be in 7-11 years old by program start date.

 

NICA Discovery Santa Fe FUNdamentals meets Wednesdays and Fridays 5:00-6:30 pm at Fort Marcy Park

September 23

September 25

September 30

October 2

October 7

October 9

 

Required Documentation

ONLINE: 

  • Registration for NICA Discovery is through the platform BikeReg.  Go to bikereg.com and search “NICA Discovery” to find your location. 

IN PERSON: 

  • Parents must print, review this CODE OF CONDUCT with their child, sign and bring it to the first session for their child to participate. 
  • Every rider is also required to have a waiver and medical release form signed on file with NICA.  A link to the waiver may be found HERE.  Parents are asked to show confirmation that the online waiver has been signed before their child participates. 

Required Equipment

  • Helmet - Helmets should be less than 5 years old with no visible cracks or defects and fit your child’s head well without moving around while they ride. 
  • Footwear - Closed-toe (non-Croc like) shoes that fastened by laces, straps or buckles
  • Bike - Bike with knobby tires, gears, and two hand brakes. Bike tires should be no smaller than 20 inches.
  • Bike repair items - A replacement tube that fits your child’s tire. (dropped off at day one check in and returned at close of program if they are un-used.
  • Snug fitting small backpack  - Kids need to be able to carry water and snacks with them at all times.
  • Snacks/Hydration - Kids should always bring a snack and hydration with them to Discovery. 
    • Examples could include a granola bar, fruit snacks, or something that can easily be stored in a pocket or pack.
    • Hydration should consist of non caffeinated sports drinks or just good ole water! 

Recommended Equipment

  • Gloves - full-finger gloves to protect hands from abrasions in the case of a fall
  • Eye protection - generic sports glasses to protect from dust and debris (and bugs) kicked up while riding
  • Windbreaker /rain jacket/coat - weather conditions change throughout the season, your child should be prepared to ride in the conditions that are present on the day. Sessions will be altered or canceled if the weather conditions are unsafe. 
  • Athletic /Cycling pants- Loose fitting athletic pants. Cycling specific shorts are not required but some kids may be more comfortable.

What to Expect

Each lesson is broken down into 3 sections.  

  • Opener activities and objective/expectation setting
  • Skills activities and Games 
  • Wrap up and Reflection

There will be a  break mid-lesson for snacking/hydrating and general check in.

Each lesson builds on skills learned in the previous one.  To get the MOST out of NICA Discovery make sure your child can attend every lesson! 

The lessons consist of riding and playing in a park-like setting and are not trail dependent. Students will ride within that open space rather than out on trails, staying close to restroom facilities and support. 

 

Kids should come ready to learn, play, ride and explore!

Backpack examples 

A small pack that fits snugly and is just big enough to carry a water bottle and snacks, and maybe a small found treasure or two is great.

Helmet examples

Bike examples 

Guide to Kids' Bike Sizing

How to determine if the bike is the correct size

Standover:

While straddling the bike with feet flat on the ground, the rider should have about 2 inches of clearance between the top tube and their inseam.

World famous Wednesday Worlds cyclocross practice at Holster Park, in Clifton NJ.

The best and only cyclocross training group in North Jersey – for over 10 years. 

Wednesday Worlds is FREE and run by local cyclocross racers. The goal is to grow the sport of cyclocross and give racers the opportunity to practice racing skills together.  We've been doing this for years and its always a good time. 

Wheels down 5:30 - Sessions are a mix of skills and drills to build fitness before moving on to FAST hard race efforts. Session ends around sunset depending on weather, daylight and conditions.  Meet at the tennis courts.  

Location:  https://www.google.com/maps/place/Holster+Park/@40.8593319,-74.188589,16z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x89c2ffb3b0eb8ab1:0xa15abc2860c1a7ec!8m2!3d40.8593319!4d-74.1860141!16s%2Fg%2F1tdwr0j4?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI0MDgyOC4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D

Important info:

  • This is a training group, not a race. Beginners are encouraged and very welcome, but be please be aware that cyclocross is physically demanding and requires a good level of fitness.   
  • We ride in a public park and conditions may change each week. We are guests in the park and will do everything to keep it clean and respect the rules.
  • We respect others in the park. We respect each other. No fighting. All are welcome.  
  • Helmet is required. Bring a cyclocross (or MTB) bike in good working order.
  • Park on the road between the school and the baseball field. Do NOT park in the fenced area behind the school.  
  • Event may be cancelled due to weather.  We ride if it rains but we cancel if stormy or if the park grounds are soaked.  Check your email and join the Facebook Group for the latest info.
  • Be nice to each other.
  • Questions? wednesdaycyclocross@gmail.com

EventNotes:
2026 Massanutten State Champs — Event Canceled

Unfortunately, we have made the difficult decision to cancel this year’s Massanutten State Champs weekend due to low registration numbers.

We announced and shared our planned date with Virginia and Maryland race directors last October in an effort to avoid scheduling conflicts, but several additional events were later added to an already crowded weekend. Ultimately, registration did not reach the level needed for us to put on the event we had planned.

All registered racers have been issues a full refund.

We’re disappointed we won’t get to race with you this year, but this isn’t goodbye to Massanutten. We’re currently looking at bringing the event back in late spring or summer 2027, and we’ll be announcing our full 2027 race schedule in October.

Thank you to everyone who registered and supported the event. We appreciate you and hope to see you at another start line soon.

2026 Virginia State MTB Championship Weekend @ Massanutten

Presented by RVA Racing Events & Massanutten Bike Park

2 Days. 3 Disciplines. One Shot at Glory.

Event runs Friday–Sunday, with optional Friday preview and packet pickup.

The Western Slope and Bike Park come alive for Virginia’s premier MTB championship weekend.
From lung-busting XCO to a brutal Over-the-Mountain Time Trial to full-send Downhill—this is where titles are earned.

Race for the podium. Ride for the story. Stay for the weekend.

WEEKEND OVERVIEW

Friday – Course Preview + Packet Pickup

Location: Western Slope – 4276 Happy Valley Rd, Keezletown, VA

Ride the course, scope your lines, and watch it come together.

4:00–7:00 PM – Early Check-In / Packet Pickup
Skip the morning rush—grab your plate and get eyes on the course.

Shuttle laps start at 4:00 PM

Saturday – XCO + Uphill Time Trial

Location: Western Slope
Day Pass Included

Expect rocks, roots, punchy climbs, and fast flow.
Half-shell helmets required

XCO

  • 8:00 AM – Check-In / Vendor Setup
  • 9:00 AM – First Wave (Non-USAC categories)
  • 10:30 AM – First Wave Awards
  • 12:00 PM – Second Wave (USAC State Championship)
  • 1:30 PM – Final Awards

Course: ~4-mile laps of classic Western Slope terrain (laps vary by category)
Route: https://www.strava.com/routes/3518781621848756736

 

Over-the-Mountain Time Trial (NEW)

Non-Championship Event

  • 2:00 PM – Check-In
  • 3:00 PM – Starts (1-minute intervals)
  • 4:30 PM – Awards

A pure test of pacing and power—go out too hot, and the mountain collects.
Same climb as last year, then down Blooming Laurel back to the start.

Uphill Time Trial Format:
Riders start individually at assigned times after registration closes.
9:00 AM race participants will start first.
Start times will be emailed and posted on Webscorer before race day.
Riders must start at their assigned time.

Route: https://www.strava.com/routes/3511844050738200932

 

Sunday – Downhill @ Bike Park

Location: Massanutten Bike Park (Ski Area)

Format: One Run, One Shot

No seeding, no second chances. Your single timed run determines the result.

Bike Park opens at 10:00 AM, and the high-speed lift will give you plenty of time for practice and pre-ride laps before racing begins.

Bike Park Access

  • Discounted passes for pre-registered riders available during registration
  • Season pass holders: you’re good
  • Required: Full-face helmet, front suspension, and disc brakes
  • Bike rentals available

Two Downhill Races

11:00 AM – Macadamia XCDH

XC-Friendly Downhill – Non-Championship Event

Fast, flowy, Western Slope-style trail—built for speed and fun.

10:00–11:00 AM: Practice / Pre-Ride
11:00 AM–1:00 PM: Racing

Route: https://www.strava.com/routes/3518781407718641152

1:00–2:00 PM – Course & Timing Transition

Timing equipment moves from Macadamia to World Cup while the course transitions for the championship race.

2:00 PM – World Cup Downhill

State Championship

Big tech, rock sections, full track. Medals are on the line.

2:00–4:00 PM: Racing

USAC license required

Route: https://www.strava.com/routes/3487524092841763052

?? 4:30 PM – Podiums & Awards

Join us at the Mid Mountain Grill at 4:30 PM for podiums, awards, and a proper end to the weekend.

Race Day at a Glance

10:00 AM – Bike Park opens / Practice
11:00 AM – Macadamia XCDH
1:00 PM – Timing & course transition
2:00 PM – World Cup Downhill State Championship
4:00 PM – Racing complete
4:30 PM – Podiums & Awards – Mid Mountain Grill
5:00 PM – Bike Park closes

Racing Saturday? Head over Sunday morning after your XCO race for practice laps. Saturday lift tickets are available at a discount during registration.

STATE CHAMPIONSHIP DETAILS

  • USA Cycling Sanctioned
  • Titles awarded to Virginia residents only (annual USAC license required)
  • Out-of-state riders may podium but are not eligible for state titles
  • Championship categories require an annual license (no one-day upgrades)

NON-CHAMPIONSHIP CATEGORIES (NEW)

Not chasing a title? Skip the paperwork and still send it.

  • No annual USAC license required
  • No one-day license required
  • Same courses. Same terrain. Same effort

There’s still a podium—just no state title on the line.

You won’t earn a jersey—but you’ll earn the ride.

NOTES & IMPORTANT INFO

  • Registration closes: Thursday, Sept 24 at 8:00 PM (no late registration)
  • Race day registration: Not guaranteed—register early
  • Timing: Chip timed with live results
  • Course marking: Fully marked and marshaled courses
  • Course support: Limited on-course support—ride prepared

Categories & Licensing

  • State Championship categories: USAC annual license required (Virginia residents eligible for titles)
  • Out-of-state riders: May race and podium but are not eligible for state titles
  • Non-championship categories: No USAC license required (annual or one-day not needed)

Downhill Format

  • One run per rider — fastest time counts
  • No second runs or combined scoring

Weather & Conditions

  • This is a mountain venue—weather can change quickly
  • Events run rain or shine unless conditions are unsafe

General

  • Helmets required for all disciplines (full-face required for DH)
  • Lift tickets for DH available during registration (Sunday required unless season pass holder)
  • Respect the course, other riders, and event staff—ride hard, ride clean

MAKE IT A WEEKEND

Bring the crew. Between races:

  • Scenic lift rides
  • Indoor water park
  • Blue Ridge views for days

Lodging discount codes will be emailed after registration.

This isn’t just a race—it’s a mountain weekend with a number plate.

Overview:
The 12th annual Fargo Sub-48 Bike Packing Adventure will take place September 25 through September 27, 2026 around beautiful northern Michigan. We're currently working on dialing in campgrounds and the routes, but we assure you it will be a great time and amazing adventure! We try to choose campgrounds in more remote and scenic areas and link them up with all kinds of adventurous terrain and scenery. Full details will be released once we have the accommodations confirmed and route fully scoped out and vetted. We check everything out well in advance to make sure it's gonna be a great time!

Participants will adventure by bike, riding approximately 40-50 miles on day one and 20-30 miles on day two, carry their camping gear, water, energy food, tools, tubes, etc...Riders should have the knowledge required to work on their bike in the event of flats, broken chains, etc.  We expect all riders to navigate the routes with a GPS device ( we'll provide GPX files) or by following the provided printed maps. The route will not be signed. 
All bikes are allowed but we highly recommend 2" and wider tires due to the sandy nature of Michigan and the rugged nature of seasonal roads and singletrack.
There is no drop bag service, no car shuttles or family moving gear for you. Tent or hammock camping only, no motor homes allowed. We will provide breakfast, lunch and dinner so carrying these meals and cooking supplies on your bike is not necessary. We encourage you to bring your own snacks for riding as convenience stores may be limited. This event is meant to be an introduction to bike packing but riders should be seasoned cyclists and capable of riding up to 50 miles with a loaded bike, in a variety of road conditions. This isn't a ride for beginner cyclists.

The 2026 adventure by bike will be limited to 140 riders with registration only through Bikereg. **Registration date is Saturday April 25th, 2026 at 9am EST. and the event typically sells out every year in less than 15 minutes. We'll email all past participants with more details and the registration opening date reminder. 

Included with your event registration:

  • Camping fees for 2 nights (Friday and Saturday)
    Friday = Location TBD
    Saturday =  Location TBD
  • Salsa Fargo Sub-48 T-Shirt
  • Free Assorted beer/seltzer and non-alcoholic options (assorted selection will be offered in cans)
  • Friday evening: Free beverages, snacks and bonfires
  • Saturday pre-ride breakfast: meal, juice, fruit, coffee
  • Saturday during the ride: aid station with a sandwich or pizza, chips, water, bars, gels, fruit....
  • Saturday post-ride: afternoon snacks, full meal with sides, Sarah Lee Pie, and beverages. We'll have plenty of firewood for bonfires
  • Sunday morning: meal, fruit, juice, coffee and shorter ride back to original campsite
  • Course maps and cue sheets
  • GPS downloadable routes for each day
  • Porta Johns

Weekend Itinerary "quick glance": (More details will be provided closer to the event weekend)

  • Friday afternoon: 4 pm rider check-in, social evening with bonfire and beverages
  • Saturday morning: 7-9 am breakfast, rider meeting, ride departure 10am
  • Saturday ride: lunch stop at approx. mile 20-25
  • Saturday afternoon: ride stop at local establishment (a la carte)
  • Saturday late afternoon: arrive at campsite, snacks and beer, full dinner around 5-6 pm,  bonfires / party
  • Sunday morning: 7-9am breakfast, riders are welcome to depart on their own schedule,
  • Sunday ride: 20-30 miles back to the cars

Route Info:

The course will be rolling, mainly dirt roads, some two-tracks and seasonal roads with sections of pavement. Depending on the weather, some seasonal roads may be dry and sandy with rutted out sections or muddy.  We recommend bikes with 2" tires or larger. The course is on roads open to auto traffic so please use caution at intersections and follow the rules of the road. 

Day 1 = 40-50 miles with some climbing        

Day 2 = 20-30 miles with some hills

Transfer your entry to a person on the wait list:
Go into your race registration and select "Edit" and  “WITHDRAW ENTRY” . Your entry will automatically be transferred to the first in line on the wait list. You’ll be refunded and see a credit to your credit card within 7 days. * please note any Bikereg fees paid during the registration will not be refunded. 

Transfer your entry to a friend:
The original registered rider finds someone to purchase their registration.  The two parties determine the price of the transferred registration and make payment arrangements on your own.  The original registered rider goes into their Bikereg entry and selects "transfer your entry" and enter the email of the person transferring in. The new rider will accept the registration, pay the $5 transfer fee and select their category.

An annual stop on the Arkansas Enduro Series, the Eureka Enduro is a rowdy weekend of racing through the "The Little Switzerland of the Ozarks" and the Victorian-style resort town of Eureka Springs. The community is home to some of the best mountain biking in Arkansas including Lake Leatherwood Gravity Park. For 2026, the Eureka Enduro is being held in conjunction with the FAT TIRE FESTIVAL, a three-day, family-friendly mountain bike festival on September 25-27, 2026.

Registration is open with participation based on a first-come, first-served basis. To create a rewarding race experience, organizers reserve the right to limit overall event participation. Each participant’s entry includes:

This event is intended to be a benefit to MORE/IMBA members! If you are not a member, you can join at the yearly rate of $39/individual or $50/family. If you are a current member and need to renew, add the membership to your cart while registering and select the member pricing for the campout. You can also always join here:

Each individual must register for the event. It does not matter how many people you have in a tent, or how many tents you have, or if you're in a RV, or whether you're an adult or kid. 

We are staying at Big Bear Lakes "Beaver Creek Village".  This is not the airstrip where they hold large events, but the camping area with a bath house shortly after the entrance. The entire campground area is reserved, there are tent sites and RV hookups at some sites. All RV and tent areas are first come/first serve and as we are a large group, expect to share sites/space with others in a "tent-city" fashion.   • Arrival is anytime Friday and departure is Sunday. If you want to arrive earlier or leave later, you need to contact Big Bear Lake Registration and make accommodations with them to purchase additional camping days. This applies whether you are tenting, or in an RV. Use this website to find the number to call to make reservations or make them online:  (Click on RV, or Tent links)
  • Sites - all RV and tent areas are first come/first serve and as we are a large group, expect to share sites/space with others in a "tent-city" fashion. There are some wooden platforms on one side of the area, not-shaded areas in the middle and an open field at the top of the area. You can set your tent up anywhere. A description of the area is here:

Cabin – there are no longer cabins at the Big Bear Lake Camplands.

Mark your calendars and join us for a local favorite - the 12 Hours of Winona and the 5th Annual Winona Lake Trail Fest presented by KCV Cycling and our friends at Lake City Restoration! Combining the fun of some of our favorite season ending events, this weekend is for the whole community with a kids night ride/scavenger hunt, trail runs, a 6 or 12 hour MTB race, and kid's MTB clinics and races as well as tours of the new bike park. EventNotes:
Watch the Instagram Page for updates and added information on the race weekend. 

This event is the finale of the  Downhill Midwest Series and the Downhill portion of the Lake Superior Gravity Series! 

This event is going to be ran similar to the big downhill races in the US. Similar to Monster Energy Pro Downhill, NW Cup, DHSE, and more. We are hoping to help give riders the experience they would get when traveling to those other races! 

The Cat 1 and Cat 2  course won't be announced until the week of the race!

Cat 3 will be on either Happy Camper or Candyland!   

For LSGS it is going to be scored the same as the rest of LSGS for that series. All you have to do is be in Cat 1 or Cat 2 to have your score count for the series. We are working with LSGS to make sure everyone's points will be counted correctly. 

Cat 3 will not be scored towards LSGS Overall as they are going to be on a separate course. But will be scored for DHMW overall.

Spirit Mountain will be offering discounted 3 day lift tickets for racers for $65 (purchased at the venue). 

Here is the schedule for the weekend!

Timing chips will be handed out at the rider meeting meeting before race runs. BE SURE YOU ARE AT THE MEETING!

Cat 1 and 2 may be split up if there are enough registrations. 

Cat 3 will be allowed to practice all day Friday and Saturday, and won't have Seeding Runs or Track Walk. Their course will also be open to the public on Friday and Saturday. 

Cat 3 youth are allowed to have parents follow them during race run. Please let us know if this is your plan. 

Have your number plate on your bike during practice. Reminder to remove the number plate before driving to prevent loosing the number plate to the wind. 

Full face helmet is required for all categories. 

Prices will go up Friday 8-28 at Midnight, and again Sunday 9-20 at Midnight. 

USA Cycling Categories

Having USA Cycling involved will help riders get into the categories they belong in for future races when they travel. Since this is one of the only USA Cycling downhill races in the Midwest (other than some collegiate racing), we will be working with riders to get into their correct category. 

Cat 1/Pro - This is going to be the fastest group of riders on the weekend. You should be very comfortable racing down the most technical features in the Midwest (ManPants in Copper Harbor, Gypsum in Marquette, Terrarium at Spirit Mountain). If you regularly are in the top 20 to 30 of the LSGS you could shoot to be in this category. 

Cat 2 - This category is for riders who feel they can ride down the more technical features in the Midwest (listed above). If you have raced the Downhill event at Copper Harbor, Marquette or Duluth before, you are certainly good enough to be in this category!

Cat 3/Novice - This category is for those who are curious about downhill racing. Maybe you've never participated in a downhill race before, or you're just getting into the sport. This category will get more practice time and will be on a separate course than the other categories. It'll be either a green or a blue trail. Dip your toes into downhill racing by being in Cat 3!

Category upgrades are done on the USA Cycling website. Not on BikeReg. You must register for the category that matches what your USA Cycling DH license is. If you have questions, I can send you a PDF to help navigate the process. 

If you have any questions please reach out. alex@downhillmidwest.com

RIDE DETAILS

Friday, September 25, 2026

Meet and check in: 9:45 AM
Mandatory rider briefing: Before departure
Ride begins: 10:00 AM

Meeting point: The designated rendezvous point on Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve, beside the Gradins olympiques washrooms and water fountain.

Please arrive prepared and ready to ride by 9:45 AM. All registered participants must attend the pre-ride briefing.

ABOUT THE RIDE

The Global Cycling Industry Friendship Ride brings together friends, colleagues and cyclists from around the world for a friendly ride through Montréal and the surrounding countryside.

This ride supports Winning The Race With Diabetes Foundation, founded by Ryan DeWald in 2016. Net proceeds from the $20 CAD registration fee will help the development of a new  WinningTheRaceWithDiabetes.org website. This new platform will allow the foundation to organize and promote future events, Share inspirational activities and personal stories, provide practical  resources for living an active life with type 1 diabetes, promote healthier lifestyles and type 2 diabetes prevention, and continue building diabetes awareness through cycling and community.

THE ROUTE

Both groups will leave the rendezvous point on Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve and ride toward the Seaway. We will stop beneath the Samuel De Champlain Bridge for a group photograph before continuing toward Sainte-Catherine.

At Sainte-Catherine, the ride will divide into two groups:

A GROUP — APPROXIMATELY 55–60 KM

Led by Ryan DeWald, the A Group will complete an additional lollipop-shaped loop through quiet country roads and scenic farmland south of Montréal. This portion of the ride will allow visiting cyclists to experience some of the beautiful roads regularly enjoyed by local riders.

The A Group will then return toward the city and may reconnect with the B Group during the return to Saint-Lambert.

B GROUP — APPROXIMATELY 35–40 KM

Led by Martin Larochelle, the B Group will follow a shorter and more relaxed route. The group will ride through the park at the end of the Seaway before turning back toward Saint-Lambert.

Both rides are social, recreational group rides—not races. Riders should choose the group that best matches their fitness, experience and preferred pace.

STRAVA ROUTE INFORMATION

The shared Strava route begins and ends beneath the Samuel De Champlain Bridge. It does not include the distance between the official Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve meeting point and the bridge. Riders should therefore follow the ride leaders and understand that their complete distance may differ slightly from the distance displayed in the Strava file.

RIDER RESPONSIBILITIES

This is a self-supported ride on roads and cycling facilities that remain open to motorists, pedestrians and other users. There will be no closed course, traffic control, support vehicle or guaranteed medical, mechanical or transportation assistance.

Every participant must:

• Wear an approved cycling helmet
• Ride a safe and properly maintained bicycle
• Follow Québec traffic laws, traffic signals and posted signs
• Follow all Parc Jean-Drapeau rules and posted speed limits
• Follow instructions from the designated ride leaders
• Ride within their personal ability and remain aware of surrounding traffic
• Carry water, nutrition, identification and basic flat-repair supplies
• Carry any necessary medications, glucose, insulin or personal diabetes supplies
• Complete the required participant acknowledgement and liability waiver

When travelling on public roads, cyclists will ride single file in groups of no more than 15, as required by Québec law. Larger attendance will be separated into additional groups. Two-abreast riding will only occur where it is legally permitted, conditions are safe and a ride leader specifically directs the group to do so.

The route, group assignments, distance, schedule and planned stops may be changed because of attendance, weather, construction, road conditions, facility restrictions, government requirements or other circumstances beyond the organizer’s control.

POST-RIDE PLANS

After returning toward Saint-Lambert, riders may gather for an optional lunch, tentatively planned for El Gordo Taco Bar. The final location will be confirmed separately. Food and beverages are not included in registration and will be purchased individually.

Depending on timing, some riders may choose to continue independently into Montréal to watch the championship racing on the Mount Royal circuit. Any activity after the organized ride has concluded is optional and is not part of the registered ride.

INDEPENDENT EVENT NOTICE

This independently organized social ride is not affiliated with, sanctioned by, sponsored by or endorsed by the UCI, the Montréal 2026 organizing committee, the City of Montréal or Parc Jean-Drapeau. References to Montréal, Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve and championship-week racing are used only to describe the ride’s location and timing.

Winning The Race With Diabetes Foundation is a United States nonprofit organization. Registration fees are not represented as Canadian charitable donations, and no Canadian official donation receipt will be issued.

Let’s ride together for friendship, healthier lives and a future in which diabetes no longer holds people back.

In the spirit of historic advances and competition between ever-evolving modes of transportation, the 3M Challenge (Muscle vs. Machine vs. Mountain) will be held on September 26, 2026. It will feature a timed challenge between two of Mountain Maryland's oldest mechanized modes of transportation, the WMSR 1309 Steam locomotive, the largest operating steam locomotive of its type in the world, and the legs of cyclists. The event will highlight the Great Allegheny Passage (GAP), Western Maryland Scenic Railroad (WMSR), the towns of Cumberland, MD, and Frostburg, MD, the scenic beauty of Allegany County, and the healthy outdoor lifestyle.

 

The Route

The Great Allegheny Passage between Cumberland and Frostburg is the only location in the country with 15.6 miles of side-by-side bike trails and scenic trains. The 3M Challenge will be a timed ride from the Western Maryland Scenic Railroad (WMSR) Station in Cumberland, MD, to the western end of the train platform at the Frostburg, MD, Depot.

• Individuals and teams (up to 6 riders) will depart Cumberland every 5 minutes, beginning as early as 9:00 AM, from the water spout on the Scenic Railway train platform at the train station at Canal Place.

The route is on Ride with GPS. https://ridewithgps.com/routes/38734043

•  Ebikes - are NOT included in this event

 

Rider Information

•  A team can have 2 to 6 riders. In the spirit of historic advances and competition between ever-evolving modes of transportation, the 3M Challenge (Muscle vs. Machine vs. Mountain) will take place on September 26, 2026.

•  All competitive challenger bicycles must be 100% human (rider) powered. There are no "e-bikes" in the competitive "Individual Rider" and "Team" categories.

•  Each team must donate a minimum of $250 to MMT. The donation per individual rider is $60.

 

About the Challenge

The challenge is to have a better climb time than the WMSR 1309 Steam Engine. Over 40 % of the riders beat the train in 2025

Individuals who beat the locomotive's climb time will receive recognition.

All participants will receive a participation Great Allegheny Passage 3M Race Shirt.  Please ensure that you fill out the form to specify your shirt size requirements.  We will try accommodating all who enter, but shirt availability is not guaranteed.

 

Purpose of the Event

Mountain Maryland Trails is a volunteer organization that collaborates with the Allegany County Government, the Great Allegheny Passage Conservancy, partner organizations, and community volunteers to manage the Maryland section of the Great Allegheny Passage trail. The efforts of the board and volunteers focus on maintaining a network of trails that promotes wellness, sustainable economic development, environmental stewardship, and connection to cultural heritage.

 

For over 30 years, the organization has played a vital role in developing the Great Allegheny Passage trail and implementing various trail improvement and safety projects, including the recently completed Borden Tunnel Lighting Project. What began as a project to reclaim a defunct rail line between Cumberland, MD, and Pittsburgh, PA, has evolved into a trail that welcomes 1.5 million visitors annually, generates approximately $800,000 in economic impact per mile of trail each year, and supports 1,393 jobs with a total labor income of $52.6 million.

 

Furthermore, the event promotes the Great Allegheny Passage Trail, which attracts tourists from around the world while also being a beloved spot for the local community.

Join the Pennsylvania Environmental Council for the 8th annual Public Lands Ride! 

The ride is a non-competitive mixed-surface event that will take place at Black Moshannon State Park and the surrounding Moshannon State Forest on Saturday, September 26, 2026. It is a celebration of bikes, community, and public lands! 

There will be three different marked courses -- 65 mile, 42 mile, and 22 mile --- all of which feature rolling climbs from rhododendron-filled stream valleys to open plateau views and a mix of gravel and snowmobile trail terrain. The 22-mile route is a great option for anyone newer to the gravel scene as the climbs are mostly very mellow and it's almost entirely smooth, maintained gravel roads. Meanwhile, the 62-mile route offers tougher climbs, more chunky bits and all the highlights of the area. And of course the 45-mile route is a nice middle ground. Because most of the courses do include some grassier and chunkier terrain, we recommend tires at least 35mm, preferably 40-45mm. E-bikes are permitted but must adhere to DCNR's guidelines for e-bike use on trails, which can be found here. 

There will be aid stations every 15-20 miles that will be stocked with real food, as well as a post-ride meal and beer/non-alcoholic beverages. All courses will be marked at turns and intersections. 

More details to come and in the meantime, check out this video from the 2022 event!

Sponsorship opportunities are available – you can find more info here or contact Molly Kestner at mkestner@pecpa.org. 

All proceeds benefit the work of the Pennsylvania Environmental Council (PEC), which facilitates trail planning, land conservation, outdoor recreation, reforestation, water protection and more across the state. Learn more about PEC's work on improving gravel riding resources in Pennsylvania here.

Franklin County Cyclists presents MICHAUX GRVL 2026

The Franklin County Cyclists are excited to once again host Michaux GRVL for 2026, and are offering 4 awesome routes with a fun scavenger hunt on all courses for everyone!

We are continuing to partner with 2 great local groups for this event; Friends of Michaux State Forest and Franklin County Cyclists. Our 2026 Beneficiaries:

         

 

MICHAUX GRVL 2026 is a ride and race to be taken at your own pace. We will be offering timing on each route for those interested in their personal statistics, and results will be posted on our website following the event. The fast may go fast & the slow may go slow. The routes we've got on tap take you through some wonderful scenery, so stop and take it in!

We recommend the use of gravel bikes with tires of at least 35mm for any route since some stretches of road can be chunky and there is a risk of punctures with smaller tires on the downhill sections of the courses.

There will be no day-of registrations, and all participants must complete their registrations on BikeReg prior to the close of the event registration. We are coordinating a pre-race packet pick up on Friday evening 6-8pm September 25, 2026 with Michaux Brewing Co. (11657 Buchanan Trail E, Waynesboro, PA 17268). AID STATION AND FINISH CUTOFF TIMES

While we want everyone to have a great time and finish the ride, we also must take into consideration the length of time our volunteer SAG motos are out on the course. Due to this, we will be STRICTLY enforcing cutoff times for Aid Stations, Food Truck, and the Finish Line. 

All Riders must cross the timing mat at the start of the ride and completion of their chosen route in order to receive an accurate ride time  The Ride Organizers will do their best to ensure that all riders who start the ride  are accounted for at the end, but it is the responsibility of the rider to make sure they either cross the mat or check in at the registration table at the completion of the ride.

Route markings for each course will be designated using signs and colored arrows ( specific to each route).  Route marking colors will be displayed at the route start. We highly highly highly recommend having a working and reliable cycling computer with GPS (Garmin, Wahoo, Karoo, etc) with the route loaded. Riders have missed our signs in the past.

GPS files for each route along with cue sheets will be available through an online link. It's strongly recommended that you use a GPS bike computer and load the files as course markings may be inaccurate due to other forces of nature (and humans).

If you need to coordinate an earlier start time, please contact us - you will not be eligible for race placing but we can still give you a time.

This is a rain or shine event and no refunds will be given, so please plan accordingly when signing up by using the BikeReg insurance if you have an eligible reason for a refund.

Participants will receive with their paid entry a meal voucher and beer/cider vouchers good towards a post ride lunch and 2 beers/ciders (ages 21+ ONLY) at a Food Truck that will be on hand that day.  Upon completion of their route, participants must take their registration ticket to the registration table to receive their meal/beer voucher. Come and Ramble with us! 

The Bicycle Coalition of Maine (BCM) and Appalachian Mountain Club (AMC) host the Maine Woods Rambler at AMC’s Medawisla Lodge in the heart of Maine’s 100-Mile Wilderness during the weekend of September 25-27, 2026! 

The focus of the weekend will be the Saturday (9/26) ride, with multiple route length options, taking riders through a nationally renowned system of logging and sporting camp access roads spread throughout the region’s rugged landscapes and flourishing wilderness. 

We’re planning a full weekend of activities and fun, including bikerafting opportunities, evening fireside chats, dark sky stargazing, and outstanding lodge meals. We hope you’ll join us for the full weekend for this unique ride and adventures in the pristine Maine Woods.

Above registration fees include food & water at multiple aid stations, an incredible post-ride meal, and 100% of BikeReg fees. Registration DOES NOT INCLUDE LODGING/CAMPING—>scroll down to view accommodation options/pricing/and reservation info.

Scroll down below to see the weekend schedule!

Route Options

  • Small – 22 miles
    Well maintained gravel roads will take you to views of clean lakes and local mountains. 100% gravel. (Elevation gain — 1,600ft) (aMTB Green Square)
  • Medium – 33 miles
    This route circles around the beautiful Roach Ponds on well-maintained gravel roads plus small sections of more rugged terrain. Capture views of the surrounding western peaks. 100% gravel. (Elevation gain — 2,100ft) (aMTB Blue Square)
  • Large – 47 miles
    Primarily well-maintained gravel roads, but will also utilize more rugged sections that some riders may feel more comfortable hike-a-biking. Rugged sections are brief but necessary to accomplish the best adventure opportunity! Spectacular vistas of the mountains, lakes, and bubbling brooks. 100% gravel. (Elevation gain — 3,700ft)(aMTB Blue Square)
  • XL – 72 miles
    This grand route will have it all and offers riders the best of what Maine AMC and other neighboring landowners offer. Be prepared for everything on the “Large” route plus more awesome gravel, more scenic views, and double the number of climbs. This route is open for riding by special permission only on the day of the event. 96% gravel. Experienced riders only: this route will include extremely difficult terrain, multiple hike-a-bike sections, additional self-support and way-finding will be necessary. Bring your A-Game, be self-reliant, ride with buddies. (Elevation gain — 6,500 ft) (aMTB BLACK due to widely variable tread surface)

***All routes are subject to change due to changing road conditions***

7 PM – Fireside s’mores, star-gazing, and friendly camaraderie!

8 AM – Breakfast (included w/ lodging or purchased separately)
Additional self-guided activities available all-day

Location

Medawisla Lodge & Cabins – Printable directions available here.

  • Cell service is limited in the Maine Woods – be sure to print or download directions before your trip.
  • GPS is unreliable north of Greenville and we recommend tracking mileage on your odometer.
  • In all seasons, accessing Medawisla requires travel on gravel logging roads and logging vehicles have the right of way. Conditions can be rough and low clearance vehicles are not recommended.
  • There is no fuel available once you leave the paved roads.

Will I have WIFI or cell service at the lodge?

There is extremely limited cell reception at the lodge and in the surrounding areas. There is a cell booster located in the lodge, however, this system is dependent on a variety of factors hence it works with varying success and is not guaranteed. There is no WIFI available at the lodge. Guests are welcome to give out the lodge phone number in.

Accommodations & Additional Meals

AMC Lodging/Camping/Meal Options Ramblers plus their friends & families are invited to spend the weekend with us! Camping and lodge accommodations are available beginning on Friday through Sunday and include breakfast, lunch, and dinner. 

Click HERE to see pricing and options for AMC accommodations and additional meals at Medawisla Lodge.

Accommodations are NOT included in the ride registration. Please book directly with AMC if you would like to stay the weekend with us. 
Online reservations are not possible for this event - you must call AMC to book accommodations. 
Call 603-466-2727 Monday – Saturday from 10:00AM – 5:00PM and reference Maine Woods Rambler, Group #747108.

Other Moosehead Region Accommodations Options: There are also many accommodations options in the Moosehead Lake region as well, ranging from 25 minutes-1.5 hours away from Medawisla Lodge. For additional lodging options CLICK HERE.

Rules and General Information

  • Helmets MUST be worn and fastened at all times while on the bike.
  • The course includes some roads open to traffic. ALL riders MUST obey all rules of the road along the course. Ride on the right at all times and single file where traffic is present. Ride predictably.
  • Traffic may include hunters, fisherman, logging trucks, and other vehicles.  
  • Riders are encouraged to wear at least one article of blaze orange; this event takes place during hunting season.
  • Though there will be an aid station(s) and limited support on the course, this area is remote so all riders should carry with them what they need including tools, parts, additional clothing, and nutrition.
  • Cyclocross, Gravel Grind, and Mountain bikes are suitable. A minimum tire width of 42mm is recommended. Err on the side of fatter tires if you are debating which of your bikes to bring. Course terrain will include smooth gravel, chunky/washed out/damaged areas, and everything in between. Minimum 48mm tire width recommended for the XL route.
  • Please let event staff know if you leave the ride for any reason. We want to ensure everyone is safe and accounted for at the end of the day.
  • Practice ‘Leave No Trace’ at all times.
  • E-bikes: Class 1, 2, and 3 e-bikes are allowed on all routes with the exception of the XL route, which allow class 1 and 3 only.
  • The XL route is being held under a special use permit issued by The Weyerhaeuser Company for use of private/gated roads not otherwise open for public use.

Cancellation Policy

Event will take place rain or shine; full refund of registration donations less a $25 non-refundable fee if made by end of day on September 4; no refunds for cancellations made after September 4. Registrations are non-transferable. Cyclists will ride at their own risk and must wear a helmet. Routes are challenging and are not recommended for beginners.

Many have enjoyed the challenge of the Savage as a “ride of passage”. Others return each year to enjoy the rural beauty of Chester and Lancaster Counties—from the simple  charm of Pennsylvania Dutch and Amish farmlands to the scenic vistas from the hills along the Susquehanna River. Warm up on rolling hills heading west of Newark DE toward Nottingham PA. Then head for steeper hills and put your training to the test on the infamous Slate Hill, Bradys Hill, Pilgrims Pathway and Furniss Road!

For those new to the Savage Century, it is recommended for the longer routes that bikes be equipped with a low gear of about 40 gear-inches (e.g. 28-tooth rear sprocket and 42-tooth chain ring on typical road bike with a 27-inch tire) or lower to prevent undue strain on the major hills. Come for the ride. Ride for the challenge!

RAIN OR SHINE EVENT

Sponsored by:

 

EVENT OVERVIEW

Nestled below the 1,143,000 Kilowatt Northfield Mountain Power Station, Kilowatt Cross returns for its THIRD year. Year-round, you can enjoy various outdoor activities at Northfield Recreation Center, such as mountain biking, cross-country skiing, hiking, and the nature center. 

Kilowatt Cross is also a part of the River Valley CX Series where there will be cumulative points across multiple races in western Mass. Other races in the series include: Blunt Park (8/24), Hydra Cross (8/31), West Hill Cyclocross Race (9/20), and Tree House CX (10/19). Categories that are part of the series are denoted in the category notes.

INCLUSIVITY POLICY

Kilowatt Cross is an inclusive race environment that is safe and welcoming to all participants, regardless of sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, race, religion, disability, or ethnic origin. 

We strive to create an atmosphere that makes all feel welcome. From Pros to first-time racers, from staff to spectators, we will not accept behavior that is deemed to be bullying or any form of harassment and violators will be asked to leave.  

At any point, if you feel uncomfortable or unsafe or see behavior that seems to be making someone else uncomfortable, please speak to an official or staff member.

FOOD and BEVERAGES

We are happy to be offering the following during the day of the race:

  • Food: El Chapincito Food Truck | MENU | 11 AM - 4 PM
  • Beer: The Brewery at North Star Farms Pour Truck | MENU | 11 AM - 4 PM

FIRST TIME RACERS

We at Kilowatt Cross value the importance of 1st time racers.  We strive to make them feel welcome and will try to ensure they have a positive first experience with Cyclocross. 

There will be an introduction clinic on Saturday, September 26th at 8 AM, open to new and beginner riders. You will ride the course and learn how to navigate the twists, turns, and obstacles. You will also learn basic skills to give you an edge on race day. You can sign up on the registration page. 

We recommend bringing a bike with wider, possibly knobbier tires than a road bike. Your mountain bike, gravel bike, fatbike, or even your commuter bike is the perfect tool! Tires that measure more than 35mm are perfect!

We welcome all questions, please message us at B2C2Cycling@gmail.com

REGISTRATION

  • Pre-registration closes on Friday, Sep 25th at 12:00 PM ET bikereg.com/kilowattcross
  • Day-Of registration starts Sunday at 7:30 AM. The price increases by $10 if there are still spots available
  • Additional races are $20
  • Registration opens at 7:30 AM, course pre-ride opens at 7:00 AM
  • Field limits for each race are posted in the race schedule.

PARKING 

Event parking will be located on the grass lawn in front of the Northfield Mountain Power Station entrance. Parking in the paved lot is for race staff only.

ON-SITE CAMPING

We are excited to offer on-site camping Friday and Saturday night, located on the grass lawn in front of the building (where event parking will be). Bathrooms will be available in the center, but no showers. Camping extends to car/van camping and tent camping. Camping fee is $30 per setup. 

PETS

Well behaved, on leash dogs are welcome on the grounds. Please have them say hi to event staff!

WARM UP and COURSE PREVIEW

  • Course pre-ride opens at 2 PM on Friday and 7 AM on Saturday
  • You may warm-up and ride the course in between races. Absolutely no pre-riding during a race.
  • If you are riding the course in between races, you must ride behind, and not pass, the last rider in the race.

STAGING and STARTING ORDER

Races will be staged with the front row according to the River Valley CX Series and then according to CrossResults Points if registered before Friday, Sep 25th. Day-of registration will be staged in the back row. 

LAPPED RIDERS

While it's ultimately a decision left to the USA Cycling officials, we do not expect to pull lapped riders this year. 

KIDS COURSE

Free! Kids will have their own course that will be open all day. No registration is required. There will not be a designated “race” time. 

RELAY RACES

The 2-person relay race will switch racers each lap. No age (other than 9+ years old) or skill requirements exist to team up. You're welcome to tag-team with your kid or BFF. 

USA CYCLING

All riders must hold a valid USA Cycling annual license or a one-day license. A one-day license can be purchased through online registration.

RESULTS

Results will be posted on crossresults.com

E-Bikes are welcome at the Seacoast Century with some caveats:
The bicycle must be pedal-assist (specifically, the bike does not move without pedaling).  E-bikes with throttle systems are not allowed.  An e-bike rider should be certain they have sufficient battery reserve for the ride they have chosen. It is the rider's responsibility to ensure that the e-bike gets back to the ride start should they run out of battery.
Event Procedure and Safety
The Granite State Wheelers(GSW) Seacoast Century is our largest ride of the year. The event is limited to 900 riders. With a flat-to-rolling scenic route along the coastlines of New Hampshire and Maine (with a few hills in our 100-mile route), and a loop into Massachusetts, the Seacoast Century is a great ride. Many riders come back year after year making this event part of their annual vacation plans.
The Seacoast Century is a relaxed family-oriented event that many choose for their first Century or return each year to enjoy with friends.
We expect basic rider courtesy and safety:
•    Calling ‘on your left’ when passing other riders and allowing a safe distance to pass.
•    Sharing the road with vehicles, obeying traffic rules, and signal our intention to turn, stop, or pass. 
•    We expect riders to travel single-file on busy road sections, where single-file is required.
•    No long pace lines – this is a ride, not a race.

We want to make great memories traveling along the scenic route that makes this event quite special. Please join the Granite State Wheelers for a memorable Seacoast Century ride, our 52nd!

Riders must follow all rules of the road, ride single file in traffic, not block roadways, and walk across bridges if so directed. Helmets must be worn at all times. The local police departments and ride ambassadors will monitor and assist riders.
Please help us to make this a safe and enjoyable experience for all. We work hard to build support with local towns and the states to offer this ride. Riders need to help us by riding safely and with courtesy to other vehicles and pedestrians to continue to offer this century.

The Seacoast Century tradition continues with a great ride that helps support bicycle safety and advocacy. Our aim is to provide an outstanding Century event that will bring you back to cycle the New England coast with us again.

We look forward to having you join us!
The Granite State Wheelers
Founded July 1971

EventNotes:
The Wild Goose Chase is a celebration of women’s cycling—and of the incredible Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge itself.

We have flat roads, little to no traffic, and expansive salt marshes that provide vital habitat for migratory waterfowl along the Chesapeake Bay. This remarkable landscape, once threatened by development, inspired Georgena Terry to launch the Wild Goose Chase in 2008. What began as a fundraiser to protect the refuge has grown into a beloved event that has raised over $190,000 for the Friends of Blackwater.

The Wild Goose Chase Bike Ride for Women takes place on and around Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge near Cambridge, MD, on the scenic  Eastern Shore. There are rides for women of all cycling levels (11,19,32, 50, and 63 miles). The ride is on Sunday. You are welcome to purchase a special edition, Ride Jersey, or purchase our outstanding ride T-shirt. We have SAG on each route and the best rest stops around that are staffed by awesome volunteers. 

Your participation in the 2026 event helps ensure the refuge can continue protecting this critical ecosystem—home to bald eagles, ospreys, migratory birds, the Delmarva fox squirrel, and so much more.

Blackwater is both a conservation success story and a place on the front lines of climate change. The more we ride through it, the more we learn from it and the more we learn how to help protect it.   

WHAT'S HAPPENING SATURDAY 

Basic Bicycle Mechanics - Join a team of women from The Rockville Bike Hub for some hands-on experience with basic bike maintenance. We will provide workshop bikes, tools and wheels for you to practice with. Topics covered will include cleaning your bike, drivetrain maintenance, brake and derailleur adjustments, bike specific tool recommendations, the crowd-pleasing flat tire repair and a few suggestions for avoiding those flats.  Dirty hands and gentle guidance guaranteed.  Workshop is about 2 hours long. We will meet in the Ed. Bldg.

Nature Rides- Look closely and you'll see it. We may see bald eagles soaring overhead, migratory birds along our Atlantic Flyway, salt marsh grasses shaping the landscape, and ghosts forests that are a powerful reminder of rising sea levels. We will keep our eyes out for animals and plants. We will meet near the entrance to the Ed. Building with bikes and helmuts. 

Bird Walks - A very knowledgable Refuge volunteer will lead us as we enjoy a pleasant morning guided hike. We will listen for the songs and catch the sightings of the special birds on the refuge. Wear shoes you can walk in, and hopefully it will not be too muddy. We will ride bikes to locations and get off the bikes and walk. Bring your own binoculars or borrow a pair, we'll have extras. We will meet near the entrance to the Education Building(Ed. Bldg).

Yoga -   Join our yogi instructor for an all-levels yoga class to stretch, activate and prepare your body and mind for a healthy ride. Bring your own mat/towel.  The class will be indoors, in a carpeted room.  The teacher will have a few extra mats. Class is 1 hour. We will meet in the Visitor Center ( about a 10 minute bike ride from the Ed. Bldg, or a 5 minute car ride)

The Harriet Tubman Ride - A guided ride to places frequented by young Harriet Tubman led by Susan Meredith who owns the Bucktown store where Harriet was a regular customer.  End at the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Visitor Center. About 15 miles and about 2 hours.   You can exit the ride early as the group passes the Ed Building on the way to the UGRR Visitor Center. We will meet near the entrance to the Ed. Bldg.

Cycling Circle- We will gather to discuss any questions you have about women cycling with our wonderful experts in the group sharing their knowledge. An hour of great discussions and great socializing.

new Gestural Sketching and Simple Watercolor Techniques - Bring your watercolors and creative mind along as we focus on the natural beauty of Blackwater Wildlife Refuge. Those with a bit of drawing experience under their belt will love this workshop where illustrator Tara Garrigan will go over the art of gestural sketching and simple watercolor techniques as we visit spots around the rfuge. Take home your memories of the ride made by your own hand. See the link here for needed materials:

new Nature Photography - Explore nature photography at Blackwater NWR with a local award-winning wildlife photographer, then hit the Wildlife Drive to capture compelling images. Smartphones welcome.  

new Guided Kayak Tour - This guided tour is through Blackwater Adventures. You will register, $25, for lunch. You will then go to the Blackwater Adventures Website to sign up for their Little Blackwater River Tour, at an additional cost. It is a fun way to experience Blackwater from the water, 2 hour tour.

Experience a relaxing paddle on the Little Blackwater River where you will learn about the marshlands of the Eastern Shore of Maryland and the critters that call this place home. The tour includes all your equipment: kayak, paddle, life jacket and paddle lesson. Layered clothing is suggested. https://blackwateradventuresmd.com/blackwater  or call Blackwater Adventures: 410-901-9255

 

new Wild Goose Chase Jersey - A specially designed Wild Goose Chase Jersey is available for purchase this year. Follow the link for Voler. They will place your order and mail your jersey directly to you. Make sure you put in your order by July 24th to have Voler send you your jersey in time for the ride in September.  Proceeds go to Friends of Blackwater. 

For more information on the jersey and how to place your order, please order directly from Voler at this link:  https://www.voler.com/custom/ordering/li/56327

Orders must be placed by July 24, 2026 to have your jersey sent to you in time for the ride in September. 

Beware of scheduling conflicts as you will not automatically be prevented from registering for events offered at the same time.

Since our venue and chef from last year were not available, we've arranged dinner through a local restaurant. This option comes at a higher cost but allows us to continue offering a great dinner and time to enjoy friends, learn from leaders in women's cycling, and maybe win a raffle.

The Pulaski MTN-X is a new multi-surface event held in Pulaski County, Virginia.  We will have three different distances--a 102 mile long course with over 12,000 feet of climbing, a 50 mile middle-distance course with just under 6000 feet of climbing, and a non-competitive 30 mile course.  All of these rides will consist of a combination of smooth asphalt, smooth gravel, and chunky gravel, although some asphalt sections will be narrow, rough and broken up.  

This will be a “timed sectors" event, which means that you won't be racing from the start gun to the finish line.  There will be timed segments throughout the course, and those are the race sectors.  Your times from each of the segments will be added together for your finishing time on which you will be ranked.  This format allows two things--foremost it allows for a safe event where riders won't be racing through stop signs and intersections.  All of our timed sectors will be on stretches of road where the rider will have the right-of-way so that no rules of the road need to be broken to race.  Secondly, it means that we can place our aid stations outside of these timed segments, so that there is no rush in filling up bottles and grabbing some snacks--those aid stations will be in untimed areas so you can wait for your friends and know that the clock is not ticking.  We think you will love this format, and it also makes for a less lonely day on the bike. 

All entry fees include a post-ride meal with a beverage and a finisher item.

Be sure to plan on coming on Friday afternoon and join us for our shake out ride on the New River Trail along with an expo and festivities at the brewery!

What hill are we climbing?

 

The Carson City Everest Challenge will climb up Kings Canyon via King St from the intersection with Longview to the trailhead parking lot at the end of the paved road. The segment is 1.45 miles long and gains 552 ft of elevation. The average gradient is 7.2% but there are section of 12% grades.

 

How long will it take?

 

Very fit riders will take on the order of 10 to 12 hours. For recreational riders the event could take quite a bit longer. We will have the course open from 3:00AM to 9:00 PM for a total of 18 hours.

 

How hard is this challenge?

 

A full Everest Challenge is a serious endurance event that requires a lot of training ahead of time. You should be able to handle being on the bike for a full day and have a good set of climbing legs. The Tour of the California Alps (The Death Ride) is another local event that would provide excellent training for the Everest Challenge.

Is the road closed to traffic during the event?

 

The road will be closed to the general public from 6AM to 6PM. During this time the only vehicles allowed on the road are King St residents, event staff vehicles, and emergency services vehicles. If family members or friends want to spectate, they are more than welcome to ride bikes up to the upperaid station, or arrange for a ride with event staff.

 

Are there aid stations?

 

Yes! There will be a full-service aid station in the trailhead parking lot at the top of King St. There will also be a water only aid station at the bottom of King St. Both aid stations will be staffed from 3AM to 11PM and have basic bicycle repair equipment.

 

What food will the aid station have?

 

The full-service aid station will be stocked all day long with water, carb drinks, energy gels, potato chips, cookies, fruit, PBJ sandwiches, various candies and sodas. We will also have catered sandwiches available for lunch from 12:00 – 2:00, as well as popsicles throughout the afternoon, and ramen noodles

and hot drinks in the evening.

 

Are there bathrooms on the course?

 

Yes, there is a set of bathrooms in the trailhead parking lot. We will also have a port-a-potty at the lower aid station.

Join us for the VeloPigs Beer and Bicycle Social Club’s 6th annual Oink At The Moon! This event is a non-competitive NIGHT GRAVEL ride taking place on the rural farm roads of western Loudoun County. 

 

Oink at the Moon Roots! 

Oink At The Moon originally began as a single, standalone charity ride in October 2020. VeloPigs’ founder, Kasey Clark, attempted to ride every gravel road in Loudoun County (over 285 miles!) in a single day. The ride was a success and raised significant funds for America’s Routes, a Loudoun-based non-profit whose mission is to protect and preserve these historic roads.

 

In 2021, to pay homage to Kasey’s big ride, the VeloPigs organized a night gravel century and opened it to club members. Each year since, Oink At The Moon has continued to grow into one of the highlights of the Loudoun County cycling calendar. It is a true grassroots gravel event, and we would love for you to come share this experience with us!

 

This year we are again being hosted by longtime VeloPig and ride leader, Brian Holesapple. He is graciously allowing us to start and end our ride at his property near Philomont.

 

Even if you’ve ridden Loudoun’s gravel before (perhaps every Saturday morning with the VeloPigs), riding at night completely changes the experience. Prepare for an exhilarating new adventure, traversing some of the lost corners of the county and camaraderie you can only find on a ride like this!

 

Ride Details

  • Routes and parking information will be emailed to you when you register.

  • The ride will take place on open roads, both gravel and paved. 

  • The ride starts at 6:30 pm, approximately half an hour before sunset, and will finish well after dark.

  • Participants are expected to follow all rules of the road and act as responsible stewards for the sport of cycling. 

  • The route will be unmarked, though GPS routes will be emailed upon registration. 

  • Road conditions will range from hardpack (almost as smooth as pavement) to sometimes deep, loose gravel with potholes and washboard. 

  • We recommend at least a 32mm tire width, though 38+ mm is ideal. We also recommend tubeless tires - changing a flat in the dark is not easy!

 

Route Options

This year, we have three route options (63 miles, 46 miles, and 30 miles – routes will be sent when you register). Unlike our Saturday club rides, these groups will not have ride leaders and are NOT no-drop. Meaning, these are drop rides. Riders are encouraged, but not required, to stick with their ride group.

The VeloPigs follow the “Mullet Protocol” for all our rides: 

  • Business at the front, party at the back. 

    • The Business is 63 miles, and the group will ride at an average speed of 16+ mph. 

    • Business Casual is 46 miles and will average 14.5-16 mph. 

    • Party Pace is 30 miles and will average 12-14.5 mph. 

  • Please register for the route and pace that will best suit your riding abilities.

  • Riders are asked to stage 5-10 minutes before the ride begins. 

  • Groups will roll out at 5-minute intervals to avoid congesting the small roads with too many riders.

 

Rest Stops

  • There are no designated rest stops, though each route passes by at least one convenience store:

    • The Business: Middleburg Safeway at mile 11, The Plains Sunoco at mile 29, and Middleburg Safeway again at mile 45.

    • Business Casual: Middleburg Safeway at mile 11, and Middleburg Safeway again at mile 29.

    • Party Pace: Purcellville 7-Eleven at mile 21.

  • Riders are expected to bring their own hydration and nutrition, and/or money to purchase more along the way.

     

Most Importantly - Food & Drink!

  • Pizza, beer (21+), and VeloPigs swag are included with entry will be provided after the ride. 

 

The Fine Print

  • Riders are expected to have appropriate fitness, equipment, and bike handling skills to complete their selected route.
  • Helmets, headlights, and taillights are REQUIRED!
    • We recommend staying with a riding buddy in case of mechanical or light issues.
  • Mechanical support will be provided before the ride by VeloPigs’ bike shop sponsor, Plum Grove Cyclery.
  • SAG support will be available for riders who experience mechanical difficulties and are unable to complete the ride.
  • Registration may be edited or transferred at no charge up until the day before the event, however refunds will not be granted.
  • If you would like to participate in this ride but are unable to cover the registration cost, please contact the Event Director.

 

Lastly, some friendly advice (because this has been an issue every year): It may be warm at the beginning of the ride, but it will get cold quickly when the sun sets! 

DRESS FOR THE COLD TEMPS AT THE END OF THE RIDE, NOT THE WARM TEMPS AT THE BEGINNING. Trust us on this….

The cyclocross cycling event is slightly different as the season runs across two calendar years starting in the fall and ending in February of the following year. Therefore CX race age is determined by an athletes racing age on DEC 31st of the year that Cyclocross season ends. CX season starts in September and goes until the end of February. A quick way to remember CX racing age is your current race age +1.

Please visit our website for venue information and racing requirements. https://www.utcx.net

UTCX is a USA Cycling-sanctioned series and follows USA Cycling’s Competition Category Policy.

Any UTCX category that is not designated as a Women’s or Junior category is open to all riders, regardless of sex assigned at birth. For the 2026 season, this gives riders 10 categories open to everyone, subject to the age and USA Cycling category requirements listed for each race.

Women’s categories follow USA Cycling’s eligibility requirements. Junior categories are based on age and sex category.

Our goal is simple: there is a place for everyone to race at UTCX, and all riders are welcome.

Farm event rules:

1. NO DOGS – Big, little, pure, mutt we love them all, but the only dogs allowed are the family farm dogs. THIS INCLUDES EVERYONE, NOT JUST CAMPERS. 

2. No open fires. You can bring your portable grills or campfire rings but no open campfires. 

3. No smoking anything.

4. Kids supervised – You’re invited and encouraged to bring your entire family to our events. We require that children have adult supervision while on the farm at all times and you, as the parent or guardian, must provide this supervision. There are 2 ponds and there will be no lifeguard on duty. Swimming is at your own risk.

RE: Kids in the pond – This is a big attraction for the youngsters and a great way for them to spend some time. However, please be aware that the boats and floating dock are the Oesterlings property and they must be treated with care. Abuse of these items or any other property will not be tolerated. Destruction of property will result in immediate ejection from the property.

5. Keep it quiet during quiet times. Quiet hours are 10pm – 7am. There will be plenty of time for you to be rowdy and loud cheering on the other racers. 

6. Don’t be a jerk.

7. Respect the property. For more than two decades now you’ve been pretty solid, which is why we keep inviting you all back. Please remember that the Oesterlings live here all year long, have been incredibly supportive of mountain biking and ‘cross racing on this property and are my in-laws! Please thank the Oesterlings for their hospitality whenever you have the chance.

8. DO NOT LITTER. I’m not just talking about around the venue where we will have some trash receptacles, but do not drop your used gel packs on the course. I know you’re quite sure that those used foil containers are going to weigh you down and keep you from winning, but if you’re caught littering the course you’ll be DQ’d (and that don’t mean I’m taking you out for a BliZzard). Put that packet back in your jersey pocket or under your leg band ’til the end of the race. The only place you will be allowed to drop the food wrappers is at the start/finish line/feed zone area where they must be picked up by a teammate or your support person. DO NOT LITTER or leave your unwanted trash or debris behind.

9. Pack out what you pack in. Going along really well with #9 above. Bring a big ol’ trash bag, put your garbage in your big ol’ trash bag, put your big ol’ trash bag in your car, put your car in your driveway, and put your trash in your trashcan at home. Thanks for helping us keep the place clean. Helping us with little things like this keeps the event going because it keeps my crew, my folks, my outlaws, and my wife happy!

10. We reserve the right to create and impose further rules or do whatever else we want!

The Ride: Gravel, Grit & Glory

Welcome to Lake Milton MTB Trails & NEO Retreat Center!

We are returning to Lake Milton for a second year, and this event would not be possible without the folks from Rust Belt Revival Trail Coalition and the neighbors at NEO Retreat Center. If you would like to camp Saturday night contact NEO Retreat Center to reserve a spot. please remember we are guests on this Christian retreat center property, and no alcohol is permitted on the property.

Due to road closures approach from 534!

Course Info

  • Race Course on Strava here.
  • Race start is at NEO Retreat Center, and is off limits until race day!
  • 6.3 miles per lap.
  • Can be ridden race direction every day for the week prior to race day.

Day Of Registration:

While we strongly encourage you to preregister (and greatly appreciate you doing so as it helps the event go more smoothly), there will be "day of" registration. It will be an extra $10 after 6pm Saturday evening, and will close 60 minutes before the start of your event.

 

Race day Schedule:

  • 9am registration/packet pickup opens
  • 9:30am Cat 3 Jr Novice U19-U13 & Kids race day of registration closes
  • 10am Cat3 Jr Novice U19-U13 & Kids race start
  • 11:30 am day of registration & number pickup closes.
  • 11:40 am Jr Novice podiums and riders Meeting
  • 12pm Cat 1 categories start
  • 12:40pm All remaining cat 2 and cat 3 categories start. THIS TIME IS APPROXIMATE!
  • 2:30-3pm, all podiums.
  • Adaptive racers, we may alter where in the schedule you start as we work with you and learn what works best. 

!!!!!!!Start time notes!!!!!

In an effort to offer a safer and more fun race environment for all participants we are now starting Cat 2 and Cat 3 racers after Cat 1 and E Bikes have completed one lap. This greatly reduces conflict between very fast cat 1 and E Bike racers passing novice racers by nearly eliminating lap traffic. The posted start time of 12:40m for cat 2 & 3 is approximate. We will begin releasing the remaining cat 2 & 3 waves after Cat 1 racers go through scoring. Know your wave number!

10am Cat3 Jr. Novice Races

You may have noticed that we are doing Cat3 Jr novice races early in the day and be asking "hey, what's up with that?" We want to give Jr's, and particularly novice Jr's the best race day experience we can. Separating the Jr. novice races to an earlier start allows us to do 3 things:

  • Fewer racers on course for the race.
  • For families where the one or both parents also race it gives the parents a chance to spectate and cheer their kids.
  • Novice Jr's get their own start, with more people cheering and spectating. Bring the cowbells!

USA Cycling Licenses, and NOMBS Series Championship rules & eligibility:

NOMBS is proud to be bringing a USAC sanctioned series to Ohio and be hosting the official USA Cycling Ohio MTB Championship. Partnering with USA Cycling helps us offer you a great series with structure, consistent categories & scoring, good insurance for landowners, and allows an opportunity for riders with goals outside Ohio to earn USAC points. 

USA Cycling Race Age:

 Your “race age” is the age you will be on December 31st. This rule exists so that a person does not have to change the age group they are entering partway through a race season. 

NOMBS Series Championship Eligibility rules:

  1. A rider must have a current USA Cycling License (need not reside in Ohio).
  2. Must race in the season finale race.
  3. Scored on best 5 races.
  4. In the event of a points tie the season final race is the tie breaker.

Complete series rules can be found here.

EventNotes:
The Tour of the Rio Grande Bicycle Century will not be an organized mass event in 2026.

For locals who are familiar with the South Valley area near the start / finish, there's been a lot of road work and construction. We have been talking with Bernalillo County and NMDOT for the past couple months in regards to the ride / permitting. They say with what is planned for Rio Bravo Blvd and its intersection with 2nd street, they cannot guarantee they will approve our permitting. They described how the state of the construction will make the road unsafe for cyclists. It is with this information I have chosen to make the event virtual.

A virtual event is one that doesn't have a particular ride date, start time or support outside of ridewithgps directions fournd on our website www.torgbc.com. This is being done so that the event holds its 4th / last Sunday of September spot on public calendars. It also gives fans of the ride the option to use the ridewithgps to find a place to park away from the construction, and attempt a part or all of the ride. There are a number of local businesses on the way that have food and beverage and they would love your support.

We did think about moving the start / finish to make the ride happen and we came to the conclusion to not change the ride in fear of ruining the experience.

Registration for the virtual tour is $5 or $20. Both options have fees and tax. The $20 dollar option will include a shirt and stickers for the virtual tour 2026 and local sponsor perks with shipping included. These will start being shipped in June and sent as they are ordered with an estimated two week turnaround time.

Online registration is open until 11:59pm MST Sunday September 27th.

SCHEDULE

RACE DETAILS

Ride Description:

  • Well marked and quiet country roads, cue sheets, SAG support, friendly volunteers and our well-stocked rest stops.
  • A non-competitive, scenic ride of 25, 50, 75 or 100 miles.
  • The first 150 riders to register get a commemorative water bottle with registration--don't miss out!!

  • Local law enforcement authorities may patrol the roads and may issue citations for traffic violations.
  • Bicycles should be ridden single file at all times, even when traffic is not present.
  • State law prohibits the use of headsets while riding on public roadways. 

This is what it's all about!
