The Relentless Run & Ruck Challenge-October 24th, 2026

The Relentless Run and Challenge is a timed competitive-style endurance event built for runners and ruck athletes. 

You can choose to run it normally (no weight) or ruck style with weight. 

Either way you're on the same trail course, pushing yourself and getting after it!! 

Course Format and Event Options: 

The Course: One, approximately 5K loop on trails.
 

Event Options: 

5K: One loop. Great for first timers, fast runners, or anyone who wants to send it.

10k: Two loops. The sweet spot- competitive, challenging, and super doable.

Relentless 6-Hour Endurance Challenge: Complete as many 5K loops as possible in 6 hours. This is the long game option: pacing, grit, and staying disciplined when it gets hard. Perfect for anyone who wants to test themself at a longer time domain/distance.

Divisions (All Distances) 

Choose a division when you register: 

Run: Run it like a normal 5K, 10K, or 6 Hour Race. No weight, just run. 

Ruck: 30lb (Men)/ 20lb (Women) 

All Ruck weights are dry weight and do not include water. See additional details below.

Scoring and Results: 

  • 5K/10K: Ranked by fastest finish time 

  • 6-Hour Endurance Challenge: Ranked by total distance completed. Tie breaker: final fastest complete loop 

    Awards/categories will be finalized based on participation 

Ruck Standards & Rules (Weighted Divisions)

Mandatory ruck weigh-in will take place before the start and at the finish line.

Weight Rules & Approved Ruck Set Up

  • Required ruck weight must be non-consumable and non-wearable. No food, water, or clothing used as required weight
  • You can carry extra supplies (food, water, layers, etc.) Just know this counts as additional weight on top of the required division weight
  • Required weight must be carried on your back as a traditional ruck. Any backpack/ruck is acceptable. Plate carriers are NOT allowed
  • No sling bags or duffel bags
  • No trekking poles allowed
  • If you have questions about your ruck set up, email katie@stay-relentless.com 

Who This Is For

The Relentless Run & Ruck Challenge is for runners who want a simple, timed event, ruck athletes who want a legit course and standards, and anyone who wants to push themselves and have some fun..

Whether you’re chasing a time, carrying weight, or just here to test yourself - this challenge is for you.

All fitness levels are welcome - come push yourself and see what you’re capable of.

Non-Profit Donations: For each participant of the Relentless Run & Ruck Challenge $20.00 will be donated to to Heroes in Transition thanks to our community impact sponsor "Alquist 3d".

 

This a Festival, it is going to be fun.

5 Points 50 is Chattanooga's oldest mountain bike race that traverses Lula lake Land Trust and Cloudland Canyon State Park trail systems across Lookout Mountain. Whether you're in it to win it or want to ride the party pace with your friends, this race has a little something for everyone! All proceeds from the 5 Points 50/25 support Lula Lake Land Trust’s trail building and maintenance. Lula Lake has built over 60-miles of trail on our properties across Lookout Mountain, including the Moonshine trails, Cloudland Connector Trail, and the Durham Mine Trails. Your participation in this race (and all of Lula Lake’s races) goes directly back into our trail maintenance and construction efforts!

Race Details:
50 Mile Course (3,500+ ft. elevation gain)
The 50-mile course starts with a 5-mile ride down Hwy 157 (Lula Lake Rd.) to the Durham Mine Trails. At Durham, racers will enjoy both single and double track trails before crossing over into 5 Points and then riding to the Ascalon trailhead. From there, riders will head back towards HWY 157 and cross over the highway to continue on the 7-mile High Point section (CCT) until you hit the Nickajack Parking Lot. Racers will then go down Nickajack road for .25miles to the F4 Trail. From here, you will ride through LLLT’s Core Preserve trails and Moonshine Trails to the finish. 

GPX file for the course 50 MILE COURSE. PLEASE BE AWARE that the mileage is not exactly accurate and the elevation could be more. This is JUST FOR REFERENCE. All racers are to follow course tape instead of the GPX file. Course markings rule the roost! The Land Trust section of the course is private and NOT to be ridden unless it is an open gate day. 

https://ridewithgps.com/embeds?id=52272426&sampleGraph=true&type=route

 

25 Mile Course (2,300+ ft. elevation gain)
The 25-mile course will begin with about 5 miles of riding down Hwy 157 (Lula Lake Rd.) to the Connector Trail road crossing, at which point you’ll turn left onto the connector trail. Riders will weave their way through LLLT’s (mostly single track) Core Preserve and Moonshine trail systems to the finish. The 25 mile course is the same as last year where it takes a left off the road onto Longbranch Connector. The 25 mile course is the second half of the 50 mile course. For the GPX file, please refer to the GPX link for the 50-mile race - the back half will be the 25-mile course. Again, follow course tape!

Join us for the fourth annual Baileys Dirt Fondo and Fundraiser on Saturday, October 24th, 2026! 

 

Our “Dirt Fondo” is adapted from a traditional Italian “Gran Fondo,” and will feature a singletrack adventure race consisting of casual riding between optionally-timed “segments” and Strava KOM/QOM segment challenges. Rest stops throughout the courses will feature local treats to keep you energized for the trail ahead. Don’t miss out on your chance to support and explore the Baileys Trail System this fall!

 

The Baileys Trail System is an 88-mile mountain-bike-optimized trail system in the Wayne National Forest. Baileys Trail System will be the longest contiguous mountain bike-optimized trail system east of the Mississippi River. Visit our website to learn more about the trail system: www.baileystrailsystem.org/

 

All proceeds from the Dirt Fondo will support the management and development of the Baileys Trail System, the work of the Outdoor Recreation Council of Appalachia (ORCA), its nonprofit partner Athens-Wayne Outdoor Asset Development Corporation (AWOADC), and our mission: "To integrate conservation, outdoor recreation, and economic development to strengthen and inspire communities in Appalachian Ohio. Learn more about ORCA and our work: www.orcaohio.com/

Race Timing:

Race segments will be automatically timed. The overall course time will be timed for the Youth/Family ride. The overall course time will be timed for Black, Blue, and Green courses, but will not be judged for the sake of scoring. 

 

Segment timing is optional and can be selected during registration. All riders will be issued a timing device and number plate. For those who elect not to be timed, your name will be removed from the final results. Use of the timing device is mandatory and will be used to manage rider safety regardless of if the rider chooses to show their name in final results.

 

Participation in the KOM/QOM segment challenge is optional. To participate, riders should record and upload their ride to Strava upon finishing. Riders must upload their ride within 30 minutes of finishing in order to be eligible for KOM/QOM prizes.

 

Participants will be issued a number plate, which should be placed on the headset/handlebars of their bike with the provided zip ties. Participants will also be issued a timing device that must be worn on the left ankle (opposite the derailleur). After the race, the participant may dispose of the timing device. The number plate can be used as a meal ticket at the finish line. Race organizers will collect number plates for reuse after they are used as meal tickets.

 

Race Scoring:

For the youth course, the team with the fastest average time will win. The top three teams will be honored on the podium. Selecting team members and a team name is required during sign-up.

 

For the Green, Blue, and Black courses, segment placement rankings will be combined into an overall score, and the individual with the lowest overall score will be the winner. Podium awards will be issued to the top 3 competitors in each category. 

 

KOM/QOM segment challenges will not be factored into overall podium placements. A prize will be issued to the top KOM and top QOM on each segment, regardless of race category. KOM/QOM participation is optional, and participants must upload their race to Strava within 30 minutes of finishing to be eligible for prizes; they must also have their Strava privacy settings updated so that segment times are publicly viewable.

Registration opens May 2026 (prices increase 7/1, 8/1, 9/1, 10/1):

  • Grand Fondue - $50, $55, $60, $65, $70
  • Half Fondue - $40, $45, $50, $55, $60
  • Mini Fondue - $30, $35, $40, $45, $50

Junior rides U19 receive a $5 discount

Sorry, NO refunds, transfers, or deferments. All no-show registration fees will be donated to Heartly House.

Start Time Windows: 7:00-8:30am (Grand); 9:00-10:00am (Half); 10:00-11:00am (Mini)

*Ride times are “rolling” which means you can start anytime during your designated time slot. This is to spread out arrival for parking and check-in, as well as keep ride groups smaller on the roads. The venue will open at 6:30am (Grand Fondue riders may start as early as 7:00am). Please do NOT arrive earlier than 6:30am

Location: Orchid Cellar Meadery & Winery - 8546 Pete Wiles Rd, Middletown, MD 21769

Distance & Elevation:

  • Mini - approx 25 miles & 2,000 ft elevation (moderate)
  • Half - approx 50 miles & 5,500 ft elevation (challenging)
  • Grand - approx 100 miles & 10,000 ft elevation (extremely challenging)

Terrain (mixed-surface): pavement, gravel, and some optional trail- Road bikes with narrow tires are NOT recommended (at least 32mm and up, treaded tires recommended)

*ALL route info, GPS files, cue sheets, and maps can be found HERE the week of the event (by Wed PM).

Aid Stations: Half (50 mile) & Grand (100 mile) routes ONLY (@ThorpeWood Barn - 13002 Mink Farm Rd, Thurmont, MD). The ThorpeWood Barn Aid Station will be open 10am-4pm.

Support: Pre-Ride bike check & support provided by Bike Doctor Frederick

Music: Matt Stowell Music will be playing (2-5pm) at Orchid Cellar Meadery

Food: La Carreta Tacos y Tortas Food Truck will be on-site (12-6pm) or bring your own 

Drinks: Mead, wine, and seltzer served by Orchid Cellar (absolutely NO outside alcohol permitted) 21+ only; non-alcoholic options are available 

Bake Sale: Assorted items will be available for purchase (donation-based) before and after the ride - participants may contribute a baked good item in return for a registration credit OR select merchandise 

Gear Swap: Bring lightly used cycling gear, parts, and accessories to donate or swap/trade (no For Sale items). Leftover items will be donated to a local cycling nonprofit organization (i.e. Bikes for the World or Phoenix Bikes)

Medical: Provided by On the Trail First Aid (Wilderness First Aid, Standard First Aid, CPR/AED, Health Care) 

Contacts: Alex & Chris Howell - Dirty Kitten Productions (fondue@dirtykittengravel.com) 240-215-4818; Bike Doctor Frederick (bikedrfrederick@gmail.com) 301-620-8868

This event benefits Heartly House in Frederick, MD: A non-profit organization that provides services, free of charge, to survivors of domestic abuse, sexual assault, intimate partner violence, human trafficking, and child abuse. Heartly House also works to develop community awareness programs and prevention education in the area. Proceeds from this event will be donated directly to Heartly House. You may choose to make an additional donation during registration.

EventNotes:
OUR FRIEND DAVE TROOP HAS BEEN DIAGNOSED WITH METASTATIC PANCREATIC CANCER. PROCEEDS WILL HELP VELO AMIS COVER THE COST OF A E-ROAD BIKE FOR DAVE!

WE ALSO HAVE SET UP A GOFUNDME PAGE HERE TO HELP DAVE AND HIS FAMILY WITH MEDICAL BILLS.  

WE HOPE THAT DAVE WILL BE ABLE TO JOIN US AT VICTORY FOR THE RIDE.

VELO AMIS PRESENTS THE FIFTH ANNUAL HALLOWEEN VICTORY TOUR 10/24/2026
ALL RIDERS GET A VELO AMIS GIFT and A FREE BEER or NON-ALCOHOLIC DRINK
(Rider Gift guaranteed for first 200 riders) 
 NEW FOR THIS YEAR, WE NOW HAVE 3 ROUTES! SEE BELOW 

NOT ROAD BIKE FRIENDLY - DON'T BELIEVE THE RIDE WITH GPS “SURFACES” 

REGISTRATION AND EVENT START:
Registration 9 am - 9:50 am
All riders must depart by 10 am

WHERE:
This scenic ride begins and ends at Victory Brewing Company in Parkesburg, Pennsylvania and will highlight a portion of the Enola Low Grade Bike Path. 

WHAT:
This ride begins and ends at Victory Brewing Company, and travels through Lancaster and West Chester counties. The routes are almost entirely on rural roads and bike paths. The Enola Low Grade Bike Path is approximately 8 miles from Victory Brewing. THE 50 and 35 MILE ROUTES HAVE MORE GRAVEL, HILLS AND SCENIC ROADS IN ADDITION TO THE ENOLA BIKE PATH.

DISTANCES:
Distances are the Halloween Victory Tour Long (50M), Medium (35M) and Short (27M). 
NOTE that the 27M is an out and back.

Routes are subject to change. Routes are not considered final until they are sent out to pre-registered cyclists following the close of pre-registration. DO NOT BELIEVE THE RIDE WITH GPS ROAD vs GRAVEL - it is NOT accurate. Believe us when we say - PLEASE DO NOT choose a road bike for this event. A gravel bike or mountain bike with a less aggressive tread would be the best choice. 

ROUTE AMENITIES:
The 27 Mile and 35 Mile routes will have 1 aid station each at approximately Mile 12 and Mile 22 respectively.
The 53M route will have 2 aid stations at approximately Mile 16 and Mile 36.
Aid stations will be well-stocked with goodies to keep you moving through the route.
The route will be well-marked, however, you are ultimately responsible, so please download maps and cue sheets and GPS files (will be sent to registered riders once online registration closes). We will NOT have Cue Sheets for you at the event, please print your own or download the PDF file of the cue sheet and save paper. The event director may alter the proposed routes due to acts of nature, road closures, and/or local recommendations. 

Remember, this is not a RACE. Enjoy a ride taking in the history and culture of Lancaster and West Chester counties with your friends, family, and perhaps new friends you meet along the way. We are riding on routes / bike paths that have many other users.  

REGISTRATION INFORMATION:
Ride is limited to 300 riders
Sorry, no refunds. Please see Route Change & Transfer Information below to see your options.  We are a 501c3 organization and your entry fee becomes a donation. Please purchase insurance through BikeReg if you are looking for a refund option.

PRICING:
$65 ($55 UNTIL 6/15/26)
Day of: $75
19 and Under: $20
Military or First Responders: Contact us for $20 registration

ROUTE CHANGE AND TRANSFER INFORMATION:
Sorry, no refunds will be available.
Transfers between cyclists are allowed via BikeReg and can be done by the registered cyclist for a $5 fee until pre-registration closes. Category changes are allowed at no charge and can be done by the registered cyclist until pre-registration closes on BikeReg, and at the event.

HALLOWEEN FUN:
It is Halloween and we encourage all riders to wear a costume for the Best Costume contest! Two winners, all riders are welcome to participate, so have fun!

THE GOODIES:
All riders will receive a rider gift (mugs guaranteed for first 200 riders), a ticket for 1 free beer / non alcoholic drink and post ride snacks. Stocked aid stations and a well marked course as well as great riding scenery!  

GPS Files/Cue Sheets:
Final Cue Sheets and GPS files/Maps/RideWithGPS will be emailed to riders within 24 following the close of online registration. Please be advised that route changes may be made depending on local requirements or local road conditions. The event director may alter the proposed routes due to acts of nature, road closures, and/or local recommendations. The route will be well-marked, however, you are ultimately responsible, so please download maps and cue sheets and GPS files. We will NOT have Cue Sheets for you at the event, please print your own or download the PDF file of the cue sheet and save paper. Make sure that you add mail@BikeReg.com to your email safe sender list.  All rider communication is through BikeReg.

WHY:
This year, know that whatever route you ride, you'll be supporting Velo Amis and our Mission. This year we will fund an E-Road Bike for Dave Troop. We will continue to support the Enola Low Grade Trail and The Hellbenders mountain bike team. Please read more about Velo Amis and our Mission and who we Support.  

Maps:  
FINAL ROUTES WILL BE EMAILED TO YOU AFTER THE CLOSE OF REGISTRATION
 

Other Rules & Guidelines:
- Unfortunately we are not able to allow “children’s bike trailers” for the ride. We feel that this ride is not appropriate for children in trailers. On the other hand, if you are riding with your child on a pull behind bike where the child is pedaling (similar to a tandem bicycle) this is allowed. We appreciate your understanding. Note that your child will need to be registered (small fee to cover insurance). Contact us to register a child on a trailer bike.
- Do not bring outside alcohol to the brewery.
- Follow the rules of the road. Routes will be open to traffic. Please, NO headphones. Please ride single file and be courteous to other users. All routes are on heavily used bicycle and walking paths. We want to be invited back, so please be good stewards!
- Bike helmet required.

*Volunteers and sponsors welcome - please contact Velo Amis by emailing lauriveloamis@gmail.com for more information on volunteering or sponsorship opportunities.

Thanks from the Velo Amis Team!

EventName: Arkansas Enduro Series | Round 3 | Gudrun Enduro @ Gudrun MTB Festival
EventNotes:
HOT SPRINGS ENDURO | OCTOBER 24-25, 2026

The Hot Springs Enduro takes place in the Northwoods Trails system located in Hot Springs National Park. This trail system houses well over 30 miles of trails ranging from beginner green trails to double black for the experts out there looking to push the limits. The AES Enduro is being held in conjunction with the Gudrun Mountain Bike Festival - a three-day mountain bike festival featuring dual slalom, Strider races and the Atilla the Hun XC races. There’s something for everyone. Come for AES and stay for the rest.

Registration opens Friday, June 12th at 8am with participation based on a first-come, first-served basis. To create a rewarding enduro race experience, organizers reserve the right to limit overall event participation. Each participant’s entry includes:

  • One-day competition with up to 4-7 stages and 10-20 total miles of rider-designed racing with dedicated pre-race practice times the day prior to the race.
  • Sufficiently marked courses with maps emailed to participants the week of the event.
  • Lively mid-race aid stations with access to professional neutral mechanics and medical support.
  • Professional event timing with accuracy to the 1000th of a second and instant results.
  • Complimentary post-race meal and cold beverages (21+ for adult beverages, ID required) in a family-friendly festival setting.
  • Awards ceremony by category with prizes awarded 5 deep.

RACE VENUE

Cedar Glades Park - Enter on Trapper Lane from Wildcat Road

Race Venue Address - 461 Wildcat Rd, Hot Springs, AR 71913

 

EVENT SCHEDULE

Final event schedule with packet pickup, official pre-ride, and start times will be released the week of the event. Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When permittable, an official pre-ride/practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances.

FRIDAY |

  • Early pre-riding is allowed although some stages may in the proccess of being finishing marking.
  • 4PM-7PM | Early Check-In | Location TBA

SATURDAY |

  • 9AM-4PM | Check-In & Official Practice Day

SUNDAY | 

  • 8AM-10AM | Timing Chip Pick-Up according to Wave Times. Late Check-In available.
  • 9AM-3PM | Race Day
  • 4PM | Podium Awards

Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When possible, an official practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances. 

 

LODGING - When it comes to lodging in Hot Springs, you have a plethora of options to choose from. From trusted hotels to cozy vacation rentals, you’ll find a perfect place to stay in Hot Springs. For a comprehensive lodging guide visit hotsprings.org.

DRY CAMPING - When possible, limited dry camping spots at the Race Venue will be available to reserve during event registration. Please refer to the event’s online registration service for additional details.

RESTAURANTS - In Hot Springs you can refuel with BBQ, pizza and a local micro brew, fresh catfish or homemade taffy. Visit hotsprings.org for a few ideas. We'd break the internet if we listed them all. 

SAFETY - This is not the time to skimp on protective equipment. Helmets are required to be worn on course during official event times and we highly suggest a full-face helmet, knee pads, and elbow pads.

TEMPERATURE - In October, Hot Springs, Arkansas, experiences mild and comfortable autumn weather. Daily highs average around 77°F (25°C), cooling down to average nighttime lows of about 53°F (12°C).

WATER & SNACKS - While hydration will be available at select locations on course, riders are encouraged to plan to carry at least 50-60 ounces of water and enough snacks to sustain themselves under strenuous exercise.

NICE TO HAVES - Bug spray, sunscreen, spare tubes, pump or CO2, plugs, patches and other parts.

DOGS - Dogs are allowed but are required to be on a leash at all times. No exceptions.

TRASH - If you pack it in, pack it out. We are guests. Please follow all event sustainability and recycling requests.

RACE DAY MEAL - A post-race meal will be provided to racers and volunteers on Race Days only. Redeemable meal tickets will be provided at the Registration & Timing tent. When possible, additional food trucks and other resources will be made available on-site for fans, family and friends.

WAIVER - All participants will be required to sign a waiver of liability prior to competing in the Arkansas Enduro Series.

REFUND POLICY - Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine, and refunds will not be issued except under extreme circumstances. The Event Organizer reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances including rescheduling the event to a future date.

If participants choose to add additional Registration Protector through BikeReg, those claims are handled entirely by Allianz Global Assistance. For policy questions or to file a claim visit www.eventregistrationprotection.com or call 1-888-799-2832.

SERIES RULES - additional series information and rules available at www.arkansasenduroseries.com/rules.

Updates: please join our Facebook page, where all updates will be made https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61578481500522                                                                                 Please join us on Instagram @pocono.cyclocross.classic

Registration: Online registration closes at 10:00PM on 10/22/26. Multiple races will cost an additional $10 for each race (the discount will be applied when you check out on Bikereg). Racers under 18 years old must have a parent sign the waiver. Day of registration is available for an additional $10 charge (cash only).  Registration opens at 8:00AM and closes 30 minutes prior to each race. No Refunds Will Be Issued.  Numbers will be on the Left Side. 

Licensing: USA Cycling Permit #TBD.  All racers must have a valid USA Cycling permit and have it with them at registration.  A one-day beginner USA Cycling license is available for $15 (cash only) at registration. 

Staging: Racers should report to the staging area, next to the skatepark, 15 minutes prior to their race.

Call ups: All pre-registered racers will receive a call up.  Call ups will be be based on the following order 1) PACX standings (first 8 in standings) 2) Crossresults standings 3) Order of registration.  Day of registration will be staged in the back of their respective category.

Lapped Riders: Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leader.  

Course: This course will be centered around a levee on the Broadhead Creek in Dansbury Park.  Riders will be on mixed surfaces, mainly grass, during the race and will be challenged by elevation changes as the course navigates on and around the levee.  There will be one run-up and one set of barriers.  The course will start with a short prologue and then run in a clockwise direction.  A full lap is approximately 2.5 KM or 1.6 miles in length.  A course preview video is available on our Facebook page and Instagram page.

Pit: A double-sided pit will be available.  Once your race is over, please remove your items.  

Team Tents: An area will be available near the pits for team tents.  There will be no cost but please message us via the ‘contact us’ button at the bottom of this page, so we can reserve your spot.  We will have 10 Team Tent spots available, which are located next to the pit. 

Parking: Please follow directions from staff.  You may be directed to park outside of the main parking area, if the main parking area reaches capacity.  Looking at the map below, we will use parking #1 first.  If we fill this up, we will then utilize parking #2.  Parking #2 provides parking, head on, in front of the Day Street Center and the basketball courts.  If needed, we will then utilize parking #3.

Rules: No alcohol permitted. No offensive language or unsportsmanlike conduct will be permitted. Helmets are required whenever you are riding a bicycle.

Restrooms: Porta-potties will be available near the start and near registration.

Timing, Results, and Podium: Timing and results will be orchestrated by Main Event Timing.  Results will be published on their website: https://my.raceresult.com/timers/4408/   A 15 minute protest period will follow the release of results.  Once the results are finalized, no changes may be made.  A podium presentation will be made following the 15 minute protest period.

Pavilion: A large pavilion, at Registration, will be available for your use.  Feel free to set-up your trainers under the pavilion. 

Title Sponsor: UESCA - United Endurance Sports Coaching Academy LLC     https://uesca.com/

When you register, you will have the option to enter to win a free coaching certification from UESCA.  This is a $599 prize that will be awarded to one lucky racer!!!   UESCA is a global leader in endurance sports education.  

Sponsors:

Pocono Bike Club        Pocono Bike Company        Lamprey Systems

Stroud Region Open Space and Recreation Commission         East Stroudsburg Borough  

Yogaversity             BevCity Brands    

Arlington Diner        U.S. Army Corp of Engineers       Shimano

ShawneeCraft Brewing Company

Thank you: We would like to extend a thank you to Mike Festa for all of his behind the scenes help.  While Town Hall Cross is on hiatus, Lamprey System's course stakes and barriers live to race another cyclocross race at PCCX; thanks Greg! A huge shout out to PACX for allowing us to be part of this long-time series.  The Pocono Bike Club is our local club; thank you for all of your support to bring this event to the Poconos. The use of Dansbury Park would not be possible without the support of East Stroudsburg Borough and the Stroud Region Open Space and Recreation Commission.  Lastly, thank you to the racers who come out and support grassroots racing!
PresentedBy: UESCA: United Endurance Sports Coaching Academy LLC

Hi all! We're very excited to see you again!  

The Great Pumpkin Ride is sponsored by the Fauquier Trails Coalition, a non-profit organization, and is a fundraiser for the construction of new trails throughout scenic Fauquier County.   

The Great Pumpkin Ride will be held October 24, 2026 this year and is a rain or shine event.  

IMPORTANT DATES: 

  • October 02, 2026 - Last day to register and guarantee shirt size
  • October 21, 2026 Last day for online transfers.
    • Emergency transfers must be requested via email after this date.
  • October 23, 2026 - Early pickup event shirt/wristband location/time - Blue Ridge Cyclery in Warrenton from 3:00pm to 6:00pm
    • You may still pickup your paperwork/shirt the morning of the event but we HIGHLY encourage you to come to early pickup. We promise you will be glad you did!
  • October 24, 2026 - Great Pumpkin Ride 2026!

IMPORTANT: In an effort to ensure everyone receives the GPR shirt they select upon registration, there will be absolutely NO exchanging of shirts at registration or at early pickup. The shirts are long sleeve performance style. Same as years past. Do your best to get the size you think you need.

Registration is online ONLY and the field is limited to 1,300 riders. Registration fee is $85.

Registration includes:

  1. ONE long-sleeved technical UNISEX shirt. There will be NO size-switching at registration!  
  2. Up to three rest stops (depending on the ride distance you select) with the Great Pumpkin foods you've come to know and love.
  3. SAG vehicles for rider support and minor mechanical issues provided.

TRANSFER RULES:

NO TRANSFERS after October 21, 2026

The Fauquier Trails Coalition does not broker transfers (we simply don’t have the volunteer staff to handle the brokering of transfers).  If you want to transfer your registration, your best bet is to post on our Facebook page.

Here is the general transfer procedure:

Replacement (new) rider –

1.  Find a rider who is looking to transfer their registration (see above).

2.  Make arrangements to pay the original rider for their entry fee.  (The original entry fee transfer must be handled separately and privately between the two parties, and outside of BikeReg.  

3.  Contact the original rider to transfer the registration to you (see instructions below)

4.  Follow the email link you receive and complete your information. Once you've completed the process, the original rider will be removed and you will be added to the list of registered participants in their place.

Original (old) rider –

1.  Find a rider who is looking for a transfer registration (see above).

2.  Make arrangements to transfer/receive payment from the new rider for your entry fee.  (The original entry fee transfer must be handled separately and privately between the two parties, and outside of BikeReg.)

3.  Go to this link: https://www.bikereg.com/great-pumpkin-ride and enter the email address of the person you're transferring your entry to.

4.  Once the new rider accepts the transfer, you will be removed from the event and the new rider will be added to the list of registered participants in your place. 

And finally . . . the roads for the Great Pumpkin Ride are NOT CLOSED!!  Please exercise caution and common sense.  If it doesn’t feel safe to ride two abreast, it probably isn’t.  And riding more than two abreast is not permitted in Virginia (and ticketing cyclists isn’t an unheard of occurrence – just be aware).

See you at the start!

Event Notes

The 12 Hours of Old El Paso or 12 HOEP is a team relay or solo racer mountain bike event held on the northeast of the beautiful Franklin Mountains, in El Paso, Texas. It is brought to you by EP Outdoor Adventures. The venue is at the Bowen Ranch Roundhouse.   This year our race will be held rain or shine on Saturday, October 24, 2026.  While this is a race, it's also an amazing day on the mountain to make new friends and spend quality time with your fellow mountain bikers as well as with any outdoor enthusiasts!

The Bowen Ranch Roundhouse has been purchased by Texas State Parks, so participants will need to get their daily access permit. If you will be camping you will also need to obtain the camping permit and display it on your dashboard. We will be verifying all permits as required by the State Park and we will do this during packet pickup to make it easier. NO PERMIT, means NO RACING! Thank you for your understanding.

COSTUMES

Besides our awesome race course, one of our greatest attractions are the costumes that our competitors come up with for the event.  They can get extremely creative with their individual or team costumes.  Prizes for the best overall costumes!

RACE START
12 hour race starts at 9:00am

The race will utilize a Lemans style start. The Lemans start ensures a safe and exciting method for starting a large number of riders. It consists of having all the riders line up at the starting line, at which time a pistol is fired. The racers will then run to their bikes, mount up, and enter the race course. All starting riders must have their bikes pre-positioned and be logged-in prior to the start of the race.  Racers that begin the race wearing a costume will get a headstart.  All riders on deck (those riders who are waiting for their teammate to complete a lap) must wait in the Pit Zone area and be ready for the transition.

RACE FINISH

The end time for the race is 9:00pm. All laps that count towards the final position standings must be completed by 8:59:59pm.  This means that if a racer finishes his lap at or after 9:00:00, the lap will not count.  The final finishing places are to be determined by the total number of laps completed and the order in which each team completed the final lap.  This means that if there is a tie in the number of laps completed, the tie breaker will be decided by who finished the laps in the fastest amount of time.

THE COURSE

The course is about 12.5 miles in length, and consists of smooth, fast flowy trail, short sections of small-to-medium rocks, fast descents, short steep climbs, mellow rolling single track, berms, gravel roads, a few arroyo crossings, and more. All-in-all it is one of the fastest, smoothest, least technical race courses in our area!

THE RULES

All participants are required to have a trail-worthy mountain bike, helmet, and bike light to compete.

Riders must be registered. No poaching please. It's rude.

Be courteous. There are plenty of passing opportunities on this course but if you must pass right this minute, please do so in a kind way. If you have a mechanical, please repair it on the side of the course and allow riders to pass easily.  All racers must conduct themselves in a civilized manner. Use of foul or intimidating language or behavior towards anyone including other racers or volunteers on or off the course will not be tolerated. Any racer found in violation of this rule will be penalized. This penalty may include the immediate disqualification of the racer and/or their team.  We're all out here having a good time!

Be a good person. No littering, help out if someone is in need, use restrooms where available, smile and say thanks to all of the great volunteers out on and off the course.

No riding in the Pit Zone.  Succinctly put, No riding in the Pit Zone.

Riders pushing bikes or slower riders must yield the right of way to racers riding bikes.

Lap Rules. When you reach the pit area, you MUST dismount your bike and approach the check-in staff before you or your partner can go out for the next lap. No check-in = No lap registered! If you decide that you are not going to continue, please let a race official know in the main pit area.

Riders who are checking out, must do so at the Check-In table in the Pit Zone.  High-five, handshake, slap, or kiss your partner to make the exchange legit. If you leave before making contact with your teammate, your team could be sanctioned with time. In general, we always want to know when you are coming or going.

Lights Required. All racers will finish in the dark, so lights are required. All participants riding at 5:00pm and after will need to use a working handlebar or helmet light. Anyone found riding with their lights off can be disqualified. Please remember to turn lights off when entering the exchange tent. 

No Headphones or Bluetooth speakers . Due to the nature of our course we need to have all of our riders alert and able to hear when other riders are approaching.

Federal, State, and local ordinances must be always followed.

All bicycles must be completely human-powered. Pedal-assist bikes or E-Bikes are not permitted on State Parks.

Pets.  All dogs must always be on leashes for the safety of the riders and everyone else.

REFUNDS/CREDITS
No refunds will be issued in case that the event must be cancelled due to uncontrollable circumstances including, but not limited to restrictions set forth by the State of Texas. The promoter reserves the right to make accommodations as it may deem fair or equitable in the event of an unexpected event cancellation.

DAY-OF REGISTRATION IS NOT AVAILABLE
On-site registration is not available, so please do not ask.  You MUST pre-register online.

PARKING
Car pooling is highly recommended as parking is limited at the Roundhouse area.

AID STATIONS

This is not a marathon race so there will NOT be any aid stations out on the course. You will be responsible for carrying enough water to sustain yourself. For solo racers (and anyone else who needs it), there will be opportunity to place water and food at the event grounds for you to grab as you pass through.

CAMPING

It's a long day on the bike, and the race doesn't end until 9:00pm, so kick back, relax, and spend some quality time with your teammates and the fat tire community. 

Primitive tent camping is permitted on State Park grounds if you are not obstructing traffic or racers.

The State Park grounds are not shaded, so if you want shade, you'll need to bring canopies and/or pop-up tents to provide shade. All tents and canopies must be secured to the ground.

We will have additional Port-o-johns for restrooms.

FOOD

A food truck will be out there in case you need to purchase some grub. 

Bring your own food and drinks.

VOLUNTEERS
Interested in volunteering? We need volunteers to help make this a successful event.  Please contact Mario Lopez lopezmario100@yahoo.com

EventName: Brutiful Cape: Gravel Bike & Fat Bike Adventure Rides - Oct 24 & 100 Miles for Fat Bikes Oct 25
EventNotes:
These are incredible gravel and fat bike rides in an area where riders get to experience all sorts of cool trails, back roads, and dirt roads that weave their way all over the Cape! Riders who select gravel rides won't be riding on beaches. Those who select fat bike options will have the opportunity to experience awesome beach riding in addition to the cool mixed terrain that this area serves up and few people know about.

For all Saturday riders who aren't camping Friday evening: We have secured parking within 0.4 mile from the campground so it won't take long to get from your car to the start!

We're offering a camping option at checkout so you can stay overnight right at the ride start & end at a nice campground if you prefer.

The Cape at this time of year is serene, it's not yet closed, but it also doesn't have many people on the beaches or trails. Roads are quieter than they are during the summer as well. 

Get your friends together to spend a fun weekend camping, enjoying the peace of the Cape, and memorable riding!

Riders will enjoy hot coffee and tea in the morning before rolling out and seasonally appropriate food (a hearty meal) at the end of the ride  (read: hot food if it's a chilly day!) Around a hot fire in a comfortable setting.

Complete details are on the Ride Page.

Well my friends, we're BACK for year SEVEN!!   

As you may know,  the HBRN8R goes beyond being just a grassroots cycling event and embodies a self-supported (mostly) test of mental, physical, and spiritual fortitude that unites participants with lasting memories and sense of accomplishment.   It's a true small-town community event that is hosted on a working farm overlooking the most beautiful ridgeline and run by the most hardworking & beautiful people (Ben & Kim Bangs).  

But here's the deal -- I'm a one-man show (and have always been).  While I appreciate the same-day support I have received over the years from friends who stepped up, it takes an IMMENSE amount of work to organize this event solo. For those of you who have been in the past, the 2-day weekend was a thing and I am so grateful to everyone's support!! Imagine putting on a wedding for 200 people by yourself two days in a row.  Crazy, I  know.  

With that said, I'm going back to our original format from the first two years - a one-day one-course format of mixed terrain riding that combines gravel, class IV, single track, farm fields, sugarhouse roads, and minimal pavement into one route that is equal to whatever bike you throw at it.   While this is mainly a self supported ride (NOT A RACE & NOT TIMED), I'll still keep your fire stoked at a few feed zones with wood-fired maple syrup, ,my homemade pumpkin chocolate chip cookies, water, and other goodies.  My buddy Jon Rutherford of ROKO vehicles will once again be out there on his Moto making sure people don't decide to snuggle up with a cuddly bear on course.   When you return, we'll spoil you with incredible locally sourced post-ride food, homemade pressed wild apple cider, a massive bonfire you can see from space where you can share stories while drinking Vermont beer.   Oh, it's been a tradition to give teddy bears and maple syrup to the first & last female/male across the line.  

The Mixed Terrain Course: 55ish miles - Coming soon!!

RWGPS:
Strava: 
GPX File: 

Bring the family because camping is FREE beginning Friday evening (a donation is welcome to support the landowners Ben & Kim) with no reservations needed!  It's a BIG ASS field.   Ben usually gives the kiddo's a tractor ride at the start of the event and lets them play in hay bails.  Oh, and there are animals to feed!  

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

But BUT Chris, the Full Harvest??  What about the MTB race on Sunday?  
I hear you loud & clear, but an official race day is out of the cards for various reasons.  The Solution?  Design the ultimate single track mtb route, give you the GPS file, assign parameters (i.e. you have all day Sunday just as long as you start/finish in the same spot),  race the course as fast as you possibly can go, and upload your time to Strava or RWGPS.  Oh and to sweeten the pot, an optional donation to the overall prize pot of local goodies that will go to the top three female & male finishers.

Note: This is not an organized day.  No food, no drinks, no feeds. Everyone must have a valid Kingdom Trails day pass on Sunday.  You assume all risks and respsonibilities.  

The MTB Course: Coming Soon

IMPORTANT NOTE: If racing the mtb course on Sunday, you are responsible of getting to the start location.  If camping at the venue, our hosts expect you to be out Sunday morning, and then you're on your own. 
 

So yeah, that's it.   Sounds fun, right?  Join us!! :-)
 

Ciao ciao for now,
Chris Gagnon
